feed.rights: Explanations and summaries are generated by AI from the original text. Dates, rates and amounts are checked against the source, but errors are still possible, so always rely on the original. Nothing here is legal, tax or investment advice.

entry.title: Minimum subpacketization of Reed-Solomon codes for cut-set-optimal linear repair
entry.summary: The Minimum Subpacketization of Reed-Solomon Codes with Linear Repair Achieving the Cut-Set Bound arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 This paper studies the smallest subpacketization of Reed-Solomon codes that allow exact linear repair of every coordinate from any d helpers while meeting the cut-set bound. It proves a lower bound of sG_s(d+1) and shows it equals sG_s(n) when d(d+2) ≥ 4(n+1). The paper also gives a finite formula for G_s(n), an asymptotic growth result, and an affine-plane example showing sG_s(n) is not universal, along with a conjecture.

entry.title: Adapting hybrid LLM inference to each request for greater efficiency
entry.summary: Request-Adaptive Execution for Efficient Hybrid LLM Inference arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 This paper presents Morph, a serving system that co-designs model architecture and runtime so hybrid language models can choose their layer layout per request. Each block pairs Attention and state space model layers, and a prefill-stage gate selects a layout that stays fixed during decoding. Experiments on six datasets report a better quality-efficiency trade-off than static hybrid baselines, with serving throughput improved by up to 3.87x and substantially lower inference latency.

entry.title: Privacy-preserving over-the-air federated learning in cell-free massive MIMO with user-centric clustering
entry.summary: Privacy-Preserving Over-the-Air Federated Learning over Cell-Free Massive MIMO System with User-Centric Clustering arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 This paper studies a cross-layer design for differentially private federated learning over cell-free massive MIMO networks, where user model updates are aggregated over the air. It shows that thermal noise in wireless reception can help mask private information, reducing or removing the need for artificial noise. The authors jointly optimize access point-user associations, transmit powers, and artificial noise variances to minimize aggregation variance under per-user privacy constraints. Simulations report up to 89% lower aggregation variance than baselines and 97% test accuracy on MNIST, with consistent gains on CIFAR-10.

entry.title: Capacity of private information retrieval from coded storage with colluding, robust and Byzantine servers
entry.summary: The Capacity of Private Information Retrieval from Coded Storage Systems with Colluding, Robust and Byzantine Servers arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 This paper studies private information retrieval from MDS-coded databases that include T colluding servers, U robust servers, and B Byzantine servers. The authors characterize the capacity for linear, full support-rank schemes and show the same expression holds without those restrictions when K=1 or T=1. They also extend the construction to retrieving P out of M files, and report that for P≥M/2 with K=1 or T=1 the multi-file scheme achieves capacity.

entry.title: Uniqueness of codes for 4-cell connected disjoint clusters in the spatial chromatic model
entry.summary: Code uniqueness of 4-cell connected disjoint clusters in spatial chromatic model arXiv · Oct 28, 2026 This paper studies the coding of the spatial chromatic model (SCM), an entity-oriented spatial data model in which each cell has a chromatic code. Earlier work had shown uniqueness for 2-cell and 3-cell connected disjoint clusters. Building on that, the authors prove that the chromatic codes of 4-cell connected disjoint clusters are unique.

entry.title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM Agent Serving
entry.summary: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper presents TAO, a scheduling framework for serving LLM-based agents that alternate between GPU model inference and external tools running on CPUs. TAO's value function combines near-term tool readiness, node-specific cache credit with time-aware decay, and token footprint, and a dynamic program jointly selects and places waiting sessions under capacity limits. Across 12 reported model-workload-concurrency settings, TAO reduces latency by up to 26.8%, mean time to first token by up to 36.3%, and increases decode throughput by up to 29.5% relative to the best evaluated baseline for each metric.

entry.title: PipeLink: Contract-Guided Linking of GPU Kernel Components
entry.summary: PipeLink: Contract-Guided Linking of GPU Kernel Components arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper presents PipeLink, a linker that combines separately compiled GPU kernel components using contracts stating what each component requires and provides. PipeLink checks these contracts, solves a joint placement of streaming multiprocessor resources, and generates the transfers between components. Across 51 configurations on Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, linked kernels run within 0.2% of the same sources compiled as one unit. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes a contract-guided linker for GPU kernel components; validated across 51 configurations within 0.2% of monolithic builds, with practical composition speedups.

entry.title: Negative Results for Over-the-Air Split Learning Under Channel Aging
entry.summary: Negative Results for Reciprocity-Based Over-the-Air Split Learning Under Channel Aging: Stability, Alignment, and Geometry arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies reciprocity-based over-the-air split learning, where channel aging rotates and attenuates the derivative signal sent back to the transmitter. Seven case studies combine numerical forecasts, mechanism checks, and competing predictions. Most predicted training accuracy gains are not supported, while some local physical relations, such as the inverse relation between amplitude and phase gradient, hold.

entry.title: Deep Holes and Aperture: Sign Laws for Lattice-Sampled Random Waves
entry.summary: Deep Holes and Aperture: Sign Laws for the Empirical Correlation of Lattice-Sampled Random Wave Fields arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies whether the empirical lag correlation of a Gaussian random wave field, sampled on a lattice within a bounded aperture, keeps a positive real part throughout the Voronoi cell. It identifies deep holes as the minimizers that govern failure and gives explicit sign-class counts for square, hexagonal, simple cubic, and body-centered cubic lattices. The authors also derive asymptotic and non-asymptotic aperture laws and state when a failure floor appears under Rayleigh-faded specular paths.

entry.title: Counting the fixed points of binary belief propagation: generic degree, syzygies, and real solutions
entry.summary: Counting the Fixed Points of Binary Belief Propagation: Generic Degree, Syzygies, and Real Solutions arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper studies how many fixed points belief propagation has on a binary pairwise model. Over complex parameters, it determines the generic degree of the algebraic family arising from finite loopless multigraphs, expressed as a graph state sum over edge sets without degree-one vertices. Two geometric realizations of this state sum are given, and at strong external fields the real fixed point count is analyzed as a lower bound. The degree, resolution, and real-count results are formalized in Lean 4.

entry.title: Wireless localization using digital twins and probabilistic inverse learning
entry.summary: Digital Twin-Guided Wireless Localization via Probabilistic Inverse Learning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies how site-specific digital twins can support wireless localization with simplified distributed infrastructure. It proposes PRISM, a probabilistic scheme using single-antenna access points, which learns a proposal distribution over user locations from channel impulse responses and reweights candidates using digital twin consistency. With 10 single-antenna access points, it reports a median error of about 0.7 m and remains effective without retraining when digital twin features are degraded.

entry.title: Contention-aware scheduling to handle skewed sparse matrix multiplication (technical report)
entry.summary: Taming Multi-Dimensional Skew in Sparse Matrix Multiplication with Contention-Aware Scheduling [Technical Report] arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This report examines why sparse matrix-matrix multiplication (SpGEMM) slows down on skewed real-world workloads. It identifies two causes: imbalance across computation cost, output density, and data locality, and cache contention from dense substructures. The authors propose adaptive morsel scheduling (AMS), which combines contention-aware load balancing, a data-conscious SMT activator, and a per-morsel hybrid accumulator. Evaluations on matrix squaring, relational queries, and graph analytics report that AMS significantly outperforms existing methods on skewed workloads while staying comparable on non-skewed ones.

entry.title: Physics-informed neural operator for channel estimation in fluid antenna systems
entry.summary: Rethinking Channel Estimation for Fluid Antenna Systems: A Physics-Informed Operator Learning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper frames channel estimation for fluid antenna systems as a stochastic inverse field-reconstruction problem constrained by the projected Helmholtz model. It shows that finite-aperture reconstruction leads to a frequency-domain deconvolution problem and proposes a U-shaped Fourier neural operator trained with a physics-aware Sobolev loss. Simulations report higher accuracy than state-of-the-art benchmarks and much lower inference latency than iterative solvers at high spatial-frequency resolutions.

entry.title: How the power delay profile threshold affects RMS delay spread estimates at 33 GHz
entry.summary: Sensitivity of RMS Delay Spread Estimation to Power Delay Profile Thresholding in Time-Varying Channels at 33 GHz arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper examines how estimates of RMS delay spread, a measure of signal time dispersion in radio channels, change with the relative power threshold applied to power delay profiles. The analysis uses wideband measurements at 33 GHz in a dynamic road environment with moving vehicles. Lowering the threshold from -20 dB to -50 dB raises the median from about 140 ns to 168 ns and the 90th percentile from 200 ns to 210 ns. Both statistics converge at lower thresholds, with -40 dB a practical convergence level.

entry.title: When Do Token Systems Stabilize? Compatibility Constraints and Community Structure
entry.summary: When do token systems stabilize? Compatibility constraints and community structure arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies token systems that enable service exchange without money, where agents face compatibility constraints. It establishes a necessary and sufficient condition for stability and shows that a minimum-token rule, selecting the lowest-balance available provider, achieves the optimal stability region. The criterion is applied to random token systems generated by stochastic block models, identifying two obstructions to stability: insufficient service opportunities for a group of communities or for an individual agent.

entry.title: Finite Fields: root sets, Frobenius maps and algebraic structure (monograph)
entry.summary: Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality and cyclic modules. It applies these tools to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory, covering cyclic and constacyclic codes, BCH and Goppa bounds, rank-metric and trace codes. It also treats character sums, Gauss and Jacobi sums, and proofs of Weil bounds, emphasizing explicit links between field, orbit and linear-dependence structure.

entry.title: Characterizing Maximum Nash Welfare: Envy-Freeness and Proportionality
entry.summary: Characterizing Maximum Nash Welfare: Envy-Freeness and Proportionality arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies how to allocate indivisible goods using the maximum Nash welfare rule. This rule was already known to be the only welfarist rule satisfying envy-freeness up to one good. The authors show that this fairness requirement can be replaced by much weaker conditions for any fixed k: envy-freeness up to k goods, or proportionality up to k goods. The characterization also holds for preference profiles with identical goods.

entry.title: Exact weight spectrum of RM(m-7,m): a counterexample to the Carlet-Solé conjecture
entry.summary: The Exact Weight Spectrum of RM(m-7,m): A Counterexample to the Carlet-Solé Conjecture arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies the weight spectrum of the Reed-Muller code RM(m-7,m), which describes which weights occur among Boolean functions of degree at most m-7. Combining affine geometry and Fourier analysis, the authors exclude eight weights previously conjectured for RM(7,14). They extend these exclusions to all m≥14 and thereby provide a counterexample to the Carlet-Solé conjecture.

entry.title: A new MIMO design using movable antennas that keeps signal paths strong
entry.summary: Design of DoF-Robust MIMO via Generalized Pinching Antennas arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper examines how distance differences between users and a base station can cause multi-user MIMO channels to lose spatial degrees of freedom. It proposes generalized pinching antennas placed close to users, which make the channel Gram matrix nearly diagonal and well-conditioned. Performance is assessed using rank-deficiency and outage probabilities. The analytical and simulation results indicate that pinching antennas can preserve spatial degrees of freedom and support users at spatially separated locations.

entry.title: Agar: What-If Analysis for Microservice Applications
entry.summary: Agar: What-If Analysis for Microservice Applications arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper presents AGAR, a counterfactual performance analysis tool for microservice applications. Instead of predicting exact values for each component, it learns simple, interpretable bounds that contain all observed behaviors and are tight enough to support end-to-end conclusions, then composes them to answer SLO-feasibility questions. This framing turns autoscaling into the query of finding the smallest resource allocation that meets an SLO. Across three microservice applications, the derived autoscaler reduces CPU allocation by up to 36.8% compared with state-of-the-art horizontal autoscalers while satisfying application SLOs.

entry.title: Noise Shapes the Surplus: Strategic Play Against No-Regret Learners
entry.summary: Noise Shapes the Surplus: Strategic Play Against No-Regret Learners arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies how an optimizer in zero-sum games can gain cumulative payoff above the minimax benchmark against no-regret learners, here Follow-the-Regularized-Leader algorithms, that act on noisy payoff scores with decaying learning rates. Passive play earns at most constant surplus, while a clairvoyant optimizer secures surplus scaling with the inverse learning rate when the mean response is profitable. Active alternating play can still extract surplus from the learner's movement when it is not, and at the canonical rate the noiseless Ω(√T) surplus is recovered under mean-zero, finite-variance perturbations. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes new exploitation mechanisms against noisy FTRL learners, proving sqrt(T) surplus under decaying rates; strong theory, but scope is limited to zero-sum games.

entry.title: Optimal and Impossible Strategyproof Facility Placement in Multiple Dimensions
entry.summary: Optimality and Impossibility in Multidimensional Strategyproof Facility Location arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies facility location in multidimensional normed spaces, aiming to minimize social cost, the sum of agents' distances to their nearest facility. For a single facility in the Euclidean plane, it shows that the optimal approximation ratios of deterministic strategyproof mechanisms match those of the coordinate-wise median, without assuming anonymity. It also shows that the coordinate-wise median is not always optimal in non-Euclidean spaces, and proves impossibility results for two or more facilities.

entry.title: Learning-Augmented Coordination Mechanisms: Using Demand Predictions to Improve Equilibrium Efficiency in Congestion Games
entry.summary: Learning-Augmented Coordination Mechanisms arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies how selfish behavior reduces efficiency in decentralized resource allocation. It proposes learning-augmented coordination mechanisms that use a possibly inaccurate demand prediction to modify resource costs, with a confidence parameter β that yields near-optimal performance when predictions are accurate while keeping a good worst-case equilibrium guarantee. The paper also gives robustness bounds and impossibility results, including limits on error tolerance in non-atomic games. ★★★★ Notable: Introduces learning-augmented coordination mechanisms for congestion games, achieving near-optimal consistency and PoS guarantees with matching impossibility results.

entry.title: JustGoal: An AI Given Only a Goal Beats Expert-Written GPU Kernels
entry.summary: JustGoal: With Only a Goal, the AI Baseline Is Above the Expert Kernels arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper introduces JustGoal, a baseline in which a general-purpose AI agent receives only an optimization goal and constraints, without kernel-specific knowledge bases or predefined workflows. On NVIDIA B200 GPUs, it beats open-source libraries on 8 of 10 operators, with per-operator geometric mean speedups of 1.14x to 2.34x, and beats the fastest public specialized-agent kernel on 5 of 9 comparable operators. The authors conclude that specialized machinery should be justified by clear gains over a same-model, goal-only baseline and reevaluated when the foundation model changes.

entry.title: Fundamental limits of bistatic ISAC over vector channels, i.e., the best achievable trade-off between communication rate and sensing accuracy.
entry.summary: On the Fundamental Limits of Bistatic ISAC Over Vector Channels arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies the fundamental performance limits of bistatic integrated sensing and communication systems over vector channels. For parallel channels with a degradation structure, the authors establish matching achievability and converse results, giving a single-letter characterization of the capacity-distortion function. For vector Gaussian channels with additive Gaussian states, they prove that Gaussian superposition coding is optimal, yielding an exact characterization of the capacity-distortion-power function. ★★★★★ Notable: Gives an exact single-letter capacity-distortion characterization for bistatic ISAC over vector channels, proving Gaussian superposition coding optimal via a Fisher-information matrix inequality.

entry.title: Thermodynamic Characterization of Message-Passing Decoders: Framework and Initial Study
entry.summary: Thermodynamic characterization of message-passing: Framework and initial study arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies the thermodynamic efficiency of message-passing decoders using the mismatch cost framework, which provides a computable lower bound on irrecoverable energy loss. Using the [7,4] Hamming code over a binary erasure channel, it shows how channel-induced initialization statistics and the step-wise evolution of the algorithmic state distribution determine the total mismatch cost. The results indicate that thermodynamic cost depends jointly on decoding dynamics, input statistics, and hardware characteristics, suggesting paths toward energy-efficient decoder design.

entry.title: INC-MoE: Overlapping In-Network Collectives with Expert Computation for Faster MoE Inference
entry.summary: INC-MoE: Overlapping In-Network Collectives and Expert Computation for Expert-Parallel Mixture-of-Experts Inference arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper presents INC-MoE, an expert-parallel mixture-of-experts layer that offloads token dispatch and output combining to the network switch and overlaps these collective operations with each other and with expert computation. In an emulated four-node deployment with a dedicated in-network computing switch, it was evaluated on OLMoE prefill with four-way expert parallelism. Relative to vLLM's default collective path, it reduces time to first token by up to 33% and raises throughput by up to 50% while matching outputs.

entry.title: Converse of symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
entry.summary: Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations arXiv · Oct 26, 2026 The paper proves the converse of the symplectic interlacing theorem. Given a global symplectic spectrum and a local symplectic spectrum satisfying the 2k-step interlacing inequalities, it constructs a real symmetric positive definite matrix with these prescribed spectra, where the local spectrum belongs to a principal submatrix. The main tool reduces s-principal compression to a rank-k singular value perturbation. In the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, the symplectic interlacing inequalities are shown to be the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem. ★★★★ Notable: Proves the converse of the symplectic interlacing theorem with a complete characterization via low-rank singular value perturbations, a notable theoretical advance.

entry.title: How learning algorithms pick equilibria and can lead to collusion
entry.summary: How Learning Selects Equilibria and When It Leads to Collusion arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 This paper studies how the design of learning algorithms affects which equilibrium players settle on in infinite-horizon discounted Markov games. It shows that stochastically stable states correspond to approximate stationary Nash equilibria that maximize the minimum transformed discounted value across players. In repeated Cournot games, every stochastically stable state yields an approximate public perfect equilibrium with minimum discounted profit above the Cournot-Nash benchmark, so collusion is inevitable under these conditions and learning dynamics. ★★★★★ Notable: Characterizes equilibrium selection via stochastic stability and proves learning dynamics inevitably yield approximate collusion in repeated Cournot games, impacting algorithmic collusion research.

entry.title: Computational Hardness of Outplaying No-Regret Learners: Easy With Pure Play, Hard Even With Mixed Play
entry.summary: The Complexity of Strategizing Against No-Regret Learners: Pure When It Is Easy, Hard Even When Mixed arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper studies how hard it is to optimize a strategy against a known online learner in repeated finite-horizon games. For general-sum games with bounded payoffs, unless P=NP, no polynomial-time optimizer can come within a constant factor cT of the best pure-action sequence, even when mixed strategies are allowed. In zero-sum games, deterministic pure actions efficiently recover surplus guarantees previously obtained only through mixed play against FTRL learners. ★★★★ Notable: Extends known hardness to broader mean-based learners and shows pure strategies match mixed surplus guarantees in zero-sum games.

entry.title: Explicit Reed-Solomon codes with optimal list and line decoding
entry.summary: Explicit Reed-Solomon Subspace Designs: Optimal List and Line Decoding arXiv · Oct 27, 2026 The paper constructs explicit Reed-Solomon codes over extension fields that can be list-decoded from a fraction 1-R-ε of errors with optimal list size O((1-R)/ε). A simpler strongly explicit evaluation-point construction achieves list size (1/ε)^O(1/ε). Both constructions admit deterministic list-decoding algorithms running in polynomial time.

entry.title: Deterministic causal quantization using shared representatives with bounded error
entry.summary: Deterministic Causal Quantization with Representative States and Bounded Error arXiv · Oct 20, 2026 The paper studies deterministic causal quantization that keeps pathwise error at most ε, where shared representatives are updated using only transmitted addresses. It compares address entropy rates with the process ε-entropy and bounds the gap for stationary sources with finite scalar ε-entropy. The authors also present results for uniform lattice grids, autoregressive Laplace and Gaussian sources, and stationary processes on finitely many centers.

entry.title: Re-examining fairness of pure Nash equilibria in Round-Robin allocation
entry.summary: Revisiting the Fairness of Pure Nash Equilibria of Round-Robin arXiv · Oct 17, 2026 The paper shows that, for additive valuations, not every pure Nash equilibrium of the Round-Robin mechanism yields an allocation that is envy-free up to one good (EF1) under agents' true valuations, correcting an earlier claim by Amanatidis et al. On the positive side, every pure Nash equilibrium of any fixed recursively balanced picking sequence mechanism is 1/2-EF1 and proportional up to one good (PROP1). The authors also give Round-Robin examples showing that no guarantee strictly better than 2/3-EF1 holds for all equilibria.

entry.title: Optimal Test for Distribution Support Size
entry.summary: Optimal Support Size Testing arXiv · Oct 14, 2026 The paper presents an optimal tester that decides whether an unknown probability distribution is supported on n elements or is ε-far from such a distribution in total variation distance. Its sample complexity is Θ(n/(ε log n)), improving on the earlier O(n/(ε log n) · log(min{1/ε, n})) bound of Ferreira Pinto Jr. and Harms (STOC 2025). The authors also provide a fairly good lower bound on support size.

entry.title: Logarithmic Separation Between LZ77 and LZ-End, and Grammar Compression
entry.summary: Logarithmic Separation between LZ77 and LZ-End and Grammar Compression arXiv · Oct 24, 2026 This paper proves a logarithmic separation between LZ77 and LZ-End. It also shows a logarithmic separation between LZ77 and grammar compression. These results establish that the compression efficiency of these methods differs by a logarithmic factor.

entry.title: Scattering Measures and Information Geometry: Describing Scattering Experiments with Finite Measures and Their Information Structure via Fisher Metric
entry.summary: Scattering Measures and Information Geometry arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The authors formulate scattering experiments as parameterized finite measures on outcome spaces and develop the information geometry defined by the Fisher metric. A scattering measure splits into total mass and normalized shape, separating Fisher information into changes in overall scattering strength and redistribution among outcomes. Measurement processes are modeled as probability or sub-probability kernels that contract Fisher information, linking the framework to optimal experimental design. The same finite-measure structure also arises in quantum measurements with incomplete detection.

entry.title: Statistical Dark Matter: Synergy Is Everywhere but Hard to Detect
entry.summary: Statistical Dark Matter: Synergy is everywhere but is hard to capture arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies synergy, an information-theoretic property found only in three or more variables jointly and absent from any subset of them. Using recent advances in multivariate information theory, the authors show synergy is far more common in complex systems than previously thought, and that it tends to dominate as the number of components grows. They also find that commonly used statistical modelling tools substantially underestimate these synergistic structures.

entry.title: Calibrating a checksum detector for bfloat16 matrix multiplication errors and its blind spots
entry.summary: Calibrating the Checksum: An Empirical False-Positive Bound for One-Sided ABFT on bfloat16 GEMM, and What It Fails to Catch arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies algorithm-based fault tolerance, a checksum method that flags corrupted matrix multiplications, which earlier work had evaluated only at float32. For bfloat16 with contraction length 4096, the authors fit a Generalized Pareto distribution to about 8e7 clean residuals and estimate a threshold near 3.14e-6 for a 1e-6 per-multiplication false-positive rate. Under their output-level perturbation model, the detector caught 304 of 400 single exponent-bit flips and none of 600 low-mantissa flips. The paper does not estimate real hardware fault rates.

entry.title: A polynomial-time test for which graphs always admit strongly EFX orientations
entry.summary: A Polynomial Time Characterization For Strongly EFX Orientable Graphs arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies fair division of discrete goods modeled as graphs, where vertices are agents and edges are goods. It gives a polynomial-time characterization of strongly EFX orientable graphs, which are graphs that admit an EFX orientation regardless of valuation. A connected graph qualifies if it is bipartite, or if its block decomposition has exactly one nonbipartite block containing a suitable degree-2 vertex whose removal leaves a bipartite graph. The authors state the proof was discovered by AI with human help in breaking the problem into subproblems.

entry.title: Simple deterministic auctions for selling multiple items
entry.summary: On the Power of Determinism in Multi-Item Auctions arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies a single buyer with multiple items whose values are independent but not necessarily identically distributed. It analyzes the approximation ratios of three simple deterministic auctions: selling items separately, selling them as one bundle, and choosing the better of the two. For two i.i.d. items, the authors derive an exact tight ratio, and for general cases they prove that optimal revenue is at most 3 times the maximum of the two simple auctions' revenues, improving earlier bounds. ★★★★ Notable: Constructs novel tight Lagrangian dual certificates resolving the iid two-item approximation ratio, and improves the multi-item revenue comparison constant from 6 to 3 with rigorous analysis.

entry.title: Geographic Incentives of Multiple Concurrent Proposers
entry.summary: On the Geographic Incentives of Multiple Concurrent Proposers arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies whether systems with multiple concurrent proposers (MCP) incentivize proposers to decentralize geographically. Proposers strategically choose locations to capture user market share, since users pick where to send transactions based on time to inclusion. The authors formally prove that proposers' quorum radii, their distance to the nearest quorum of attesters, determine their incentives, so proposers minimize this radius. This yields co-location when proposers also act as attesters, but geographic diversity when those roles are separate. Pre-confirmations and faster intervalidator connections are shown to weaken the quorum radius effect and further destabilize co-location incentives.

entry.title: Approximate uniformity in finite convolution models: how closely a sum of two fixed-support distributions can mimic the uniform law
entry.summary: Approximate Uniformity in Finite Convolution Models arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies how well the sum of two independent distributions with fixed support can approximate the uniform law. It measures closeness using Manhattan distance, Euclidean distance, forward Kullback-Leibler divergence, and the line-metric Wasserstein-one distance. Explicit results are obtained for two models, including one conjecture. The authors also apply their reconstruction method to a recent conjecture about the coding capacity of an additive noise channel.

entry.title: Surrogate-enhanced fractional programming for MIMO device-to-device interference management
entry.summary: Surrogate-Enhanced Fractional Programming for MIMO Device-to-Device Interference Networks arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper addresses weighted sum-rate maximization in multi-stream MIMO device-to-device interference networks. It extends the scalar surrogate-enhanced fractional programming (SEFP) method to matrix ratios using Hermitian functional calculus, yielding a matrix SEFP framework. The authors show XMMSE is a special case of SEFP and propose SEFPLinQ for joint scheduling and beamforming, with numerical results reporting consistent gains.

entry.title: Sunflowers of Reed–Solomon Codes: Families of Codes Sharing a Common Intersection
entry.summary: Sunflowers of Reed--Solomon Codes arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 The paper introduces Reed–Solomon sunflowers, families of Reed–Solomon codes whose pairwise intersections all equal the same fixed subspace. It gives an algebraic criterion using generalized V-matrices to identify such families. The authors study their sizes through counting and constructions, fully resolving the dimension-two case. For higher dimensions they give recursive and greedy constructions with many petals.

entry.title: Heddle: Learning Structural Templates for Parallelism Planning on Heterogeneous GPU Clusters
entry.summary: Heddle: Learning Structural Templates for Parallelism Planning on Heterogeneous GPU Clusters arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 Heddle is a learning-based planner for training large machine learning models on heterogeneous GPU clusters. It reduces the planning problem to searching over pipeline structures, learning offline to build plans from structural templates across diverse cluster configurations. Evaluation reports that Heddle matches or exceeds the best of five existing planners, with throughput gains of up to 84.5% on dense models and 4.6x on MoE models.

entry.title: Efficient Transmit Waveform Design for 1-Bit DAC MIMO-OFDM Radar-Communication Systems
entry.summary: Efficient Transmit Waveform Design for MIMO-OFDM DFRC Systems with 1-Bit DACS arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies transmit waveform design for MIMO-OFDM dual-functional radar-communication systems that use 1-bit digital-to-analog converters, a topic it describes as underexplored. The waveform is designed to maximize the trace of the target angular Fisher information matrix, subject to symbol-error constraints via constructive interference and a 1-bit time-domain alphabet. The resulting large-scale nonlinear integer problem is solved with an inexact ADMM algorithm that alternates between time- and frequency-domain updates. Simulations show promising radar-communication performance.

entry.title: HARS: An LDPC bit-flipping decoder that sets parameters from the initial syndrome and local reliability
entry.summary: HARS: LDPC Bit-Flipping Decoding With Initial-Syndrome-Conditioned Parameter Mapping and Local-Reliability Weighting arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents HARS, a bit-flipping decoder for LDPC codes that combines local channel reliability with parameter selection based on the initial syndrome. The initial syndrome weight sets the base weight, reliability coefficient, threshold decay factor, and perturbation amplitude for each frame. On rate-one-half PEGReg and WiMAX codes, HARS reduces bit-error rate and mean iteration count compared with a calibrated SM-NGDBF baseline. An FPGA implementation on an XC7A200T is also reported.

entry.title: A study of the maximum number of DNA sequences distinguishable by single-label DNA labeling
entry.summary: On the Capacity of DNA Labeling in the Single-Label Setting arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 DNA labeling distinguishes DNA sequences by recording where labels appear, and its labeling capacity is the growth rate of the number of distinguishable sequences as length goes to infinity. The authors model the labeling process as a deterministic channel and show its zero-error capacity equals the labeling capacity. For a single label this channel is a star graph, and they derive zero-error capacities for all star graphs, fully characterizing single-label cases. They also present a general method for constructing capacity-achieving codes.

entry.title: Nonlinear data pricing makes optimal revenue computable again
entry.summary: Non-Linear Pricing Restores Tractability for a Data Seller arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies how a data seller should price multiple datasets for budget-constrained buyers, using pricing functions that map purchased quantity to total payment. Prior work showed that optimal linear pricing is computationally intractable. The authors show that allowing general monotone, lower-continuous pricing functions can raise revenue and makes the optimum computable in polynomial time. Optimal functions are piecewise linear and convex, with total kinks bounded by the number of buyers.

entry.title: Why Walker satellite routing tables are not periodic, and how to compare them with fiber
entry.summary: On the Lack of Periodicity of Walker Satellite Constellation Routing Tables arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper models the configurations of a Walker satellite constellation as a dynamical system given by a translation on a torus, and extends this analysis to routing through satellites and fixed ground relays. For any deterministic, time-invariant routing rule, the routing table is periodic when the ratio of angular speeds is rational and non-periodic but ergodic when it is irrational. Long-run averages can then be computed from an explicit invariant measure, which makes comparisons of round-trip times between the constellation and terrestrial fiber meaningful.

entry.title: ParaAnya: A plug-and-play output cache that speeds up parallel diffusion sampling by reusing repeated computations.
entry.summary: ParaAnya: Accelerating Parallel Diffusion Sampling with Plug-and-Play Output Caching arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Diffusion model sampling is inherently sequential and computationally expensive. Parallel-in-time solvers use sliding windows, which causes the same timesteps to be evaluated repeatedly. ParaAnya caches input-output pairs and reuses them at overlapping timesteps, dispatching only cache misses to GPU workers. On Stable Diffusion v1.5 with eight GPUs, it gives 1.30 to 2.43 times speedups over uncached samplers and reduces function evaluations by up to 70.1% while keeping CLIP scores comparable.

entry.title: Optimal rank-metric quantum codes and their exact recovery radii
entry.summary: Singleton-Optimal Rank-Metric CSS Codes : Equality Structure and Exact Projected-Recovery Radii arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies rank-metric quantum codes for correlated faults that are dense physically but low-rank over a base field. It proves an asymmetric rank-metric Singleton bound for CSS codes, including degenerate ones, and characterizes equality via commuting maximum-rank-distance matrix codes. For Singleton-optimal pairs with positive logical dimension, the measured syndrome exactly determines the projected error modulo stabilizers at radii strictly below half the sector rank distance.

entry.title: Selecting Contributors for Regional Digital Twins with Coverage Guarantees While Vehicles Move
entry.summary: Conditional-Coverage Contributor Selection for Regional Digital Twins Under Mobility arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies how regional digital twins coordinate which contributors may join over congested broadcast networks in mobile settings without fixed infrastructure. The authors propose a host-coordinated protocol that admits only contributors whose timely, non-redundant coverage gain exceeds a congestion price within a cycle deadline, using a 13-byte beacon digest for pre-transmission scoring. Standards-based simulation reports that the timely actionable coverage deficit drops from 5.6% to 1.4% at comparable load to ETSI redundancy mitigation.

entry.title: Algorithm for Arctic product-mix auction equilibria
entry.summary: Solving the Arctic Product-Mix Auction arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies Arctic product-mix auctions, where budget-constrained bidders express preferences over multiple substitute goods. It gives the first strongly polynomial algorithm for finding competitive equilibria when the auctioneer has separable convex piecewise-linear costs. The method combines a strongly polynomial reduction to the costless Arctic auction with an existing strongly polynomial algorithm for that case. ★★★★ Notable: Gives the first strongly polynomial algorithm for competitive equilibria with convex costs, plus reductions to Fisher and Arrow-Debreu markets, with rigorous theoretical support.

entry.title: Incentive-compatible online matching with random arrival order
entry.summary: Arrival-Time Incentive Compatibility in Random Order Online Bipartite Matching arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper studies random-order online bipartite matching where users care only about being matched, while the platform maximizes total reward. It proposes the first constant-competitive, arrival-time incentive-compatible edge-weighted algorithm on complete bipartite graphs. The competitive ratio depends on the imbalance factor between online and offline nodes. For binary rewards, the authors present algorithms with a strictly better ratio.

entry.title: LDPC Fractus Codes: Sparse Codes Built by Recursion
entry.summary: LDPC Fractus Codes: Sparse Codes with Recursive Structure arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper introduces Fractus matrices, sparse matrices built through a self-similar recursive process, and uses them to construct LDPC codes. The resulting Tanner graphs have girth six and guarantee a minimum Hamming distance of at least ℓ+1. The authors establish algebraic properties of these matrices, including sparsity, regularity, recursive decomposition, and a natural lattice structure.

entry.title: Influence maximization in near-linear time: a faster method for choosing key seed nodes
entry.summary: Maximizing Social Influence in Almost Linear Time arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies influence maximization, which seeks k seed nodes in a graph with n nodes and m edges to maximize expected information spread under standard diffusion models. The prior Borgs et al. algorithm ran in Õ((n+m)k) time, and later work only reduced log factors or improved the dependence on ε. The authors present an algorithm achieving a 1−1/e−ε approximation in Õ(n+m) time, removing the multiplicative dependence on k from the running time. ★★★★★ Notable: Resolves an open problem by removing the k factor, achieving near-linear time with the 1-1/e-epsilon guarantee; substantial theoretical advance with broad subfield impact.

entry.title: Voronoi-Markov chain and spatial entropy for point pattern analysis
entry.summary: Voronoi-Markov chain and spatial entropy for point pattern analysis arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper revisits entropy in a spatial setting to derive computable, interpretable metrics for point pattern analysis, such as in histopathology. It reviews stochastic point process assumptions like Poisson homogeneity and Simple Sequential Inhibition, along with Voronoi and Delaunay tiling results that can provide null distributions for hypothesis testing. The authors introduce a "dense basin entropy" based on the Ord distribution over Voronoi basins, which is sensitive to clustering, and a Markov chain approximating Brownian motion. Simulations and histopathology experiments show these metrics offer insights complementary to other spatial entropy measures.

entry.title: Fundamental Limits of Dynamic Tracking and Communication via Stationary Policies
entry.summary: Fundamental Limits of Dynamic Tracking and Communication: A Stationary Policy Formulation arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies joint sensing and communication, where a multi-antenna transmitter communicates with a receiver while tracking a moving target. The sensing-communication trade-off is formulated as a rate-distortion problem, with a tractable outer bound on tracking error derived via the posterior Cramér–Rao bound. Under stated assumptions, stationary randomized Markov policies are shown to suffice, leading to a Gaussian covariance-control outer bound. Numerical experiments compare this outer frontier with an achievable frontier based on an extended Kalman filter.

entry.title: DNN-Assisted Near-Optimal SCMA Codebooks for Rician Fading Uplink Channels
entry.summary: DNN-Assisted Near-Optimal Codebook Design for Uplink SCMA Schemes over Rician Fading Channels arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper addresses Sparse Code Multiple Access (SCMA), a non-orthogonal multiplexing technique for next-generation networks, and proposes a deep neural network (DNN)-assisted method for designing near-optimal uplink codebooks. The DNN is trained unsupervised, using a loss function derived from codebook structural characteristics, so no labeled data is required. Rician-factor-dependent design criteria are derived, with AWGN and Rayleigh fading as limiting cases, along with upper and lower bounds on average mutual information. Numerical results show gains over representative benchmark schemes across a range of Rician factors and good error-rate performance in the error-floor region.

entry.title: A hyperbolic bound on how fast two files can be retrieved from DNA storage
entry.summary: A Hyperbolic Bound for File Retrieval in DNA-Based Data Storage arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper studies how sharing coding redundancy between two files affects their expected retrieval times in DNA-based storage. It focuses on two files encoded by a systematic linear code over a finite field. The authors prove a conjecture that the sum of each file's dimension divided by its expected retrieval time is at most one, provided one file has dimension greater than one. The proof uses a geometric view of growing spans and a sharpened projection bound.

entry.title: Satellite semantic communication with vector quantization and index compression for high-resolution remote sensing images over AFDM
entry.summary: Dual-Branch Vector-Quantization-Aided Satellite Digital Semantic Communication with Index Compression for High-Resolution RSI Over AFDM arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper proposes DVQ-SDSC, a dual-branch vector-quantization-aided satellite semantic communication framework for transmitting high-resolution remote sensing images over affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM). It processes high-frequency residuals and low-frequency structural semantics separately, and reduces index bitrate using PCA-based codebook reordering and group DPCM (G-DPCM) coding. Experiments on FAIR1M over 3GPP NTN-TDL-D channels show it outperforms the JPEG-LDPC scheme at 0.0625 bits per pixel.

entry.title: Sharing downstream profits with data sellers in tree-shaped data markets
entry.summary: Profit Reallocation Mechanisms in Tree-based Data Trading arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 Data can be copied and resold repeatedly, forming tree-shaped chains of resale, while upstream sellers capture none of the downstream value, which weakens their incentive to trade. The paper develops a framework for profit reallocation on such tree-structured markets, introducing a sequential trading game and a class of budget-feasible reallocation mechanisms, along with efficient algorithms for computing equilibria. The authors prove that any budget-feasible mechanism weakly expands equilibrium trades, and budget-balanced mechanisms also weakly improve social welfare. Experiments on synthetic markets show these benefits grow with the tree's depth and branching.

entry.title: Competitive optimality of Bell-Cover randomization in testing by betting
entry.summary: Competitive optimality in testing by betting via Bell-Cover randomization arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper extends the Bell-Cover randomization result to testing by betting for composite nulls and simple alternatives. It shows that the randomized numeraire e-variable UE* beats any other e-variable with probability at least one half. The authors prove this competitive optimality is equivalent to the numeraire inequality E_Q[E/E*] ≤ 1, and they discuss its costs in expected log wealth and power.

entry.title: A truthful-in-expectation method for fairly splitting indivisible items, guaranteeing a constant share of each agent's maximin value
entry.summary: Truthful-in-Expectation Mechanism with Constant Maximin-Share Guarantee arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper studies fairly allocating indivisible goods among n strategic agents with additive valuations. The authors give a randomized mechanism that is truthful in expectation and guarantees each agent at least 1/7 of her maximin share in every realized allocation. The mechanism is also ex-ante envy-free and runs in polynomial time. This confirms a conjecture that cardinal information allows a constant ex-post MMS guarantee. ★★★★ Notable: Resolves a conjectured gap, giving a truthful-in-expectation mechanism with constant ex-post MMS guarantee and polynomial-time implementation.

entry.title: Dynamic wakeup when collisions are costly: a randomized algorithm
entry.summary: Dynamic Wakeup under Costly Collisions arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies the wakeup problem on a shared communication channel, where packets become active at arbitrary times and a transmission succeeds only when exactly one packet sends. The authors propose Lowball, a randomized algorithm that needs neither collision detection nor knowledge of the number of packets. They measure performance by both latency and a per-collision cost C, and show that for large C the expected latency and expected collision cost are O(C^{1/2+ε} ln C) and O(√C).[ ]

entry.title: A simple proof of the group-theoretic Zhang-Yeung inequality
entry.summary: A simple proof of the group-theoretic Zhang-Yeung inequality arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper addresses the Zhang-Yeung inequality, the first non-Shannon-type inequality valid for all entropic vectors. Earlier work showed a one-to-one link between linear entropy inequalities and multiplicative inequalities on subgroup cardinalities of finite groups, but a direct group-theoretic proof of Zhang-Yeung was missing. The authors give a direct proof of this group-theoretic version using elementary group-theoretic and counting arguments.

entry.title: Memory in the Sky: Drone Memories Combined to Answer Low-Altitude Questions
entry.summary: Memory in the Sky: Low-Altitude Question Answering with Multi-Agent Memory Aggregation arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies low-altitude question answering (LAQA), where memories gathered by several drones are combined at a ground server to answer questions about long-term observations. It proposes a generative adversarial exam (GAE) to measure memory quality and a memory-centric framework (MemCen) that jointly selects drones and allocates transmit power under communication limits. MemCen reports QA accuracy of 92.4% and 84.0% in CARLA Town04 and Town05, and 88.5% on the PMAS real-world benchmark.

entry.title: Binary k-center with a hard threshold, applied to delegated voting
entry.summary: Binary k-Center under a Hard Threshold with Applications to Delegated Voting arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper studies covering binary strings of equal length, some possibly with missing entries, using a fixed number of center strings so that each input is within a given relative distance of its closest center. It is motivated by multi-issue approval voting, asking how representatives should be designed before an election so that as many voters as possible are willing to delegate. The authors give a complete picture of computational complexity across the number of centers and the agreement threshold when entries may be missing. For the case without missing entries, they extend the hardness results to any number of centers and large thresholds, leaving a narrow threshold range unresolved.

entry.title: Online resource allocation where budgets can be refilled
entry.summary: Online Resource Allocation with Replenishable Budgets arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Online resource allocation is a framework for sequential decisions under budget limits, usually assuming budgets can only decrease. This paper studies a more general setting where actions can either consume or replenish resources, motivated by inventory systems and energy markets. The authors propose a dual-based algorithm that recovers best-of-both-worlds guarantees in the standard case and improves them when the replenishment factor is positive. It achieves Õ(√T) regret in stochastic settings and Õ(√T) α-regret in adversarial settings, and strictly satisfies budget constraints.

entry.title: Truthful-in-expectation fair-share allocation of chores with a constant guarantee
entry.summary: Truthful-in-Expectation MMS Allocations for Chores arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies how to allocate indivisible chores fairly while keeping truthful reporting incentives in expectation. It presents the first such mechanism that guarantees a constant ex-post maximin share approximation for any number of agents, achieving 4/3 for two agents and 3/2 for three. For two agents, the authors raise the known lower bound to 4/3, showing their mechanism is optimal there. For any n of at least 3, they prove a lower bound of 13/12 on the achievable ratio.

entry.title: Weaver: A System Using Idle GPU Capacity at AI-RAN Sites to Train Foundation Models
entry.summary: Weaver: A System for AI-RAN Compute Sharing with Foundation Model Training arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper studies spare GPU capacity in AI-RAN cell sites, finding that 40-85% of GPU capacity goes unused, and that this spare capacity is complementary across sites. The authors present Weaver, which trains foundation models alongside radio access network workloads without degrading RAN performance, using a compute-aware MAC scheduler and elastic training. According to the paper, the prototype creates up to 4.9x more usable spare compute, and a multi-site testbed shows 2.1-3.7x higher training throughput than baselines.

entry.title: Finite-Resolution MiLAC-Aided Multiuser Beamforming
entry.summary: Finite-Resolution Microwave Linear Analog Computer (MiLAC)-Aided Multiuser Beamforming arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies multiuser beamforming with a microwave linear analog computer (MiLAC), whose tunable elements can take only finitely many states instead of continuous values. Under lossless and reciprocal constraints, it jointly optimizes discrete susceptances and power allocation, and designs codebooks from channel statistics. The authors propose exact continuous penalty models, proven globally equivalent to the discrete problems, and ADMM-based algorithms. Numerical results show a 3-bit stem-connected MiLAC reaches over 95% of the sum-rate of an unquantized fully-connected MiLAC using only 22% of its tunable components.

entry.title: Envy-free splits of random assignments, with four agents solved
entry.summary: Envy-Free Decompositions of Random Assignments: Settling Four Agents, and What Lies Beyond arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper studies whether a random assignment of objects to agents can be decomposed into deterministic assignments so that every agent envies any other with probability at most 1/2. It proves this is always possible for four agents using a computer-aided check over all vertices, and shows 1/2 is the best general threshold. It also gives proofs for special cases and shows some natural decomposition methods fail. Deciding whether an arbitrary random assignment admits such a decomposition is strongly NP-complete. ★★★★ Notable: Settles the open four-agent case with a complete computer-aided proof and proves strong NP-completeness, a high-novelty result with limited practical impact.

entry.title: AReaL-TIK: An agent that optimizes unified RL GPU kernels using a search-tracking representation
entry.summary: AReaL-TIK: Stateful Agentic Optimization of Unified RL Kernels through an Optimization IR arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 Reinforcement learning post-training often uses separate GPU kernels for rollout and policy updates, and numerical differences can distort probability ratios. The paper introduces KernelBraid, an agentic framework that starts from a hand-tuned, bitwise-consistent unified kernel and organizes code search with an optimization intermediate representation. Changes are kept only if they pass correctness checks and improve aggregate latency. Across 12 end-to-end training setups on H20, it reaches 1.10x average throughput relative to AReaL with log-probability recomputation. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes an agentic optimization framework with an IR for bitwise-consistent RL kernels, validated across 12 end-to-end configs and multiple operators.

entry.title: Does AI Advice Help or Harm Decisions? Study of Information Gathering with AI Input
entry.summary: Does AI Help or Harm? Endogenous Information Acquisition with AI Advice arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies how AI advice given before a costly information-gathering step and final decision affects decision quality, measured by the gross utility of the final action. It characterizes gross effects through the value function generated by optimal acquisition under uniformly posterior-separable costs. The authors show that convexity of this value function is necessary and sufficient for every AI signal to weakly improve gross utility at every prior, while nonconvexity can allow harm. ★★★★ Notable: Characterizes when AI advice weakly improves decision quality via convexity of continuation value, with tight state-space results and counterexamples; theoretical, with limited empirical grounding.

entry.title: Tighter limits for constant-power and low-power error-correcting cooling codes
entry.summary: Improved bounds for constant-power and low-power error-correcting cooling codes arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies binary constant-power and low-power error-correcting cooling codes for on-chip buses, which correct errors while controlling power and thermal effects, with e=w-3. The authors extend the earlier Zhao and Zhang upper bound for CPECC codes from w≥2t(t+1)+2 to w≥w0(t), where w0(t) is about √2·t^(3/2), and use Steiner systems to show this bound is attainable and asymptotically tight. For LPECC codes they give a new upper bound, ⌊C(n+2,3)/C(w+t,3)⌋, valid for w≥μ(t) with μ(t) about √2·t^(3/2), which is strictly smaller than the previous bound where both apply and is asymptotically tight.

entry.title: Autonomous AI system finds new kissing number constructions in 19 dimensions
entry.summary: Large-Scale Autonomous Discovery of Kissing Number Constructions arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The kissing-number problem asks how many non-overlapping spheres can touch a central sphere, and exact values are known only in a few dimensions. The authors used the autonomous multi-agent system Qiushi Engine to obtain new lower bounds in nineteen dimensions. Each result is supported by explicit mathematical arguments and independently checkable finite certificates. Examples include K(25)≥197580 and K(55)≥53301140. ★★★★ Notable: Gives new kissing-number lower bounds in nineteen dimensions via varied constructions with checkable finite certificates, though improvement magnitude over prior work needs full-text confirmation.

entry.title: A proof of the generalized packing-covering conjecture (a coding-theory conjecture now proven)
entry.summary: A proof of the generalized packing-covering conjecture arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper proves the generalized packing-covering conjecture for linear codes. The conjecture states that the t-th generalized Hamming weight is at most twice the t-th generalized covering radius plus two. The proof is computer-assisted, combining a parity-check reformulation, length bounds on possible counterexamples, and puncturing arguments. All orders t ≥ 32 are settled, and the remaining finitely many cases are excluded by exact computer verification. ★★★★ Notable: Proves a long-standing conjecture via parity-check reformulation, length bounds, puncturing, and exact computer verification of remaining cases.

entry.title: Monitoring Multitenant Kubernetes Clusters with TLA+ Trace Checking
entry.summary: Monitoring and Verification of Multitenant Kubernetes Clusters using TLA+ Trace Checking arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper presents a monitoring tool that uses TLA+ trace-checking specifications at runtime, rather than only for design-time model checking. The tool infers system behavior from Kubernetes audit logs and detects violations in it. Its primary use case is multitenancy violations, though the pipeline is not limited to that setting. The work shows how formal reasoning can be incorporated into live Kubernetes environments to improve monitoring and correctness checking.

entry.title: A method for synthesizing safe update schedules for safety-critical systems
entry.summary: Synthesizing Update Schedules with Game-Based Extension of Bounded Model Checking arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper addresses how to apply software updates to safety-critical systems without interrupting operation or using cold spare hardware. The authors model the system and the update as a two-player timed game and use a bounded SMT encoding to synthesize a fixed global-time update schedule. The schedule is claimed to guarantee safe and complete deployment under all admissible system behaviors, demonstrated on an autonomous driving trajectory planner.

entry.title: WaveAlign: Cache-Aware Query-Row Scheduling for Faster Sparse Attention in Long-Video Generation
entry.summary: WaveAlign: Cache-Aware Query-Row Scheduling for Sparse Attention in Long-Video Generation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 Long-video generation with diffusion transformers produces very long token sequences, so attention becomes the main inference bottleneck. The paper proposes WaveAlign, a lightweight framework that reorders query rows in dynamic sparse attention, grouping rows by similar key/value access patterns and sorting them within GPU waves to improve L2 cache hit ratio and reduce HBM traffic. Because only query and mask rows are permuted, sparse-attention semantics and existing kernels are unchanged. Reported results across two GPUs, two video DiTs, and four sparse-attention methods include up to 1.25x kernel and 1.17x end-to-end speedup without quality loss.

entry.title: Divergence-minimizing distribution matching for parallel and memory channels
entry.summary: Divergence-Minimizing Distribution Matching for Parallel Channels and Channels with Memory arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper extends distribution matcher theory to distributions with memory and shows that the divergence-minimizing matcher selects the highest-probability target sequences, as in the memoryless case. A divergence scaling law is generalized to distributions driven by innovation processes. The theory is applied to parallel additive white Gaussian noise channels using a modified enumerative sphere-shaping method with a weighted energy constraint. A three-channel example shows that joint shaping across channels substantially reduces rate loss at short blocklengths compared with product matchers, and simulations with probabilistic amplitude shaping and a 5G-NR LDPC code confirm the gains.

entry.title: Robust beamforming for OTFS massive MIMO under uncertain channel information, with GPU acceleration
entry.summary: GPU-Accelerated Robust Beamforming for OTFS Massive MIMO with CSI Uncertainty arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies robust beamforming for OTFS-based massive MIMO systems when channel state information is uncertain. The authors minimize total transmit power under a chance constraint that guarantees a set outage probability, and model the uncertain channel with support vector clustering as an asymmetric uncertainty set. They convert the problem into a semidefinite program and design a GPU-accelerated parallel ADMM algorithm. Simulations reportedly show lower transmit power than conventional schemes and a speedup from the GPU-accelerated ADMM.

entry.title: Automatic self-reduction gives stronger randomized distributed lower bounds
entry.summary: Distributed Lower Bounds via Automatic Self-Reduction arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies randomized lower bounds for graph problems in the distributed setting. The authors show that self-reduction is a special case of classical round elimination and introduce a new error measure under which round elimination yields bounds beyond ω(log log n). They identify a class of problems where this improvement applies black-box. The paper proves Ω(√log n) randomized lower bounds for maximal matching on regular 2-colored graphs, 1/k-integral matching, and maximal H-packing. ★★★★★ Notable: Unifies self-reduction as a special case of classical round elimination, yielding black-box randomized lower bounds beyond ω(log log n) with clear novelty.

entry.title: Robust Resource Management for Satellite-Air-Ground Networks Using Neural Network Channel Uncertainty Learning
entry.summary: Robust Resource Management for SAGIN using DNN-Driven Channel Uncertainty Learning arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies joint robust beamforming and resource allocation in space-air-ground integrated networks when channel state information is uncertain. It formulates a chance-constrained problem that minimizes total transmit power while meeting user quality-of-service requirements under a set outage probability. A deep neural network learns the uncertain channel as an asymmetric uncertainty set, and an adaptive iterative algorithm jointly optimizes resource allocation and beamforming. Simulations show the method achieves better energy efficiency and robust reliability than traditional robust and non-robust approaches.

entry.title: Covert communication over large fluid antenna arrays: how channel hardening affects detection
entry.summary: Covert Communications over Enormous Fluid Antenna Systems (E-FAS): Impact of Channel Hardening on Detection arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies covert communication over enormous fluid antenna systems (E-FAS), where guided surface wave propagation creates a channel with a random covariance scale. With a passive warden present, the optimal likelihood ratio test reduces to an energy detector, and the authors derive its false alarm and missed detection probabilities. Numerical results show that finite-mode E-FAS channels improve covertness over the fully hardened Rayleigh limit for finite observation intervals. The effect of channel hardening is asymmetric across the legitimate and warden links.

entry.title: Computational complexity of multi-agent binary-action contract design, mapping approximation limits within gross-substitutes rewards
entry.summary: Settling the Complexity Landscape of Multi-Agent Contracts with Binary Actions arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies how hard it is to compute optimal contracts when several agents each choose between two actions, focusing on gross-substitutes reward functions and related classes. The authors show the problem is APX-complete even for OXS rewards, and they give an EPTAS for weighted matroid rank functions, with no general randomized FPTAS. For partition matroid rank functions they give an FPTAS. For ultra reward functions, they prove that no polynomial-time randomized value-query algorithm achieves a 2^{o(n)} approximation in expectation. ★★★★ Notable: Maps a fine-grained approximability landscape within gross substitutes, with rigorous APX-completeness, EPTAS, and FPTAS results.

entry.title: Torch-PIM: Profile-guided automatic decisions on offloading PyTorch code to memory-near compute
entry.summary: Torch-PIM: Automated Profile-Guided PIM Offloading for PyTorch arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper presents Torch-PIM, a compiler framework that uses profile-guided optimization to decide whether each parallel loop in PyTorch-generated code runs on the host CPU or on processing-in-memory (PIM) hardware. Each loop is assessed by its amount of work and its memory boundedness, using host profiling or information from MLIR. The authors report speedups over CPU-only execution of up to 8.6x on tensor operators, 2.9x on MLP, 4.4x on Attention, 5.1x on GPT-J-6B, and 3.6x on LLaMA-7B across PIM configurations of 32 to 128 cores.

entry.title: Contraction of Rényi divergences for discrete channels (how Rényi divergences shrink through noisy channels)
entry.summary: Contraction of Rényi Divergences for Discrete Channels arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper studies strong data-processing inequality (SDPI) constants for Rényi divergences on finite spaces, examining how they depend on the Rényi order. It proves monotonicity and convexity properties, identifies support restrictions on the relevant distributions, and gives bounds relating the constants to χ² and Hellinger divergences. The results are applied to local differential privacy and to finite-time convergence bounds for Markov chains. ★★★★ Notable: Systematically characterizes Rényi-SDPI constants on finite spaces, with monotonicity, convexity, support restrictions, and tensorisation bounds, applied to LDP and Markov chains; strong theory.

entry.title: Nash Equilibria in Pacing-Strategy Auctions: Complexity and Inefficiency
entry.summary: Nash Equilibria in Auctions with Pacing Strategies: Complexity and Inefficiency arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper studies Auctions with Pacing Strategies (APS) games, where utility-maximizing bidders across many simultaneous first-price auctions each choose one pacing multiplier that scales their bids. It shows some instances have no approximate pure Nash equilibrium and that deciding whether an equilibrium exists is NP-complete in general but polynomial when the number of bidders or items is fixed. When equilibria exist, both the Price of Anarchy and the Price of Stability are exactly e/(e-1). ★★★★ Notable: Introduces APS games, proves non-existence of approximate pure equilibria, NP-completeness, and exact tight inefficiency bounds; strong theory, narrow subfield impact.

entry.title: Semantics, Workflows, and Infrastructure: How Production AI Agents Are Served at Scale
entry.summary: Semantics, Workflows, and Infrastructure: Understanding Agent Serving at Production Scale arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper analyzes a two-week trace of 11.7 million requests from a large-scale production platform for general-purpose AI agents, supported by inference infrastructure with over 10,000 GPUs. It examines the platform at three connected levels: task initiation semantics, workflow execution patterns, and infrastructure serving demands. The measurements reveal highly skewed request volumes across sessions, rare execution overlap among sibling requests, and context reuse across task boundaries. The authors then discuss deployment implications and open problems for future agent serving systems.

entry.title: How partition shape and rank density affect the speed of distributed quantum circuit simulations
entry.summary: The Shape of Speed: Impacts of Partition Geometry and Rank Density in Distributed Quantum Circuit Simulations arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper evaluates 764 validated configurations of 39-qubit distributed quantum circuit simulations on 1,024 nodes of the Fugaku supercomputer. It finds that torus partition geometry dominates runtime, with flat partitions running 1.73 to 2.31 times slower than near-cubic ones despite identical data transfer. Rank density is a secondary factor, reducing runtime by about 11% at 16 ranks per node only on compact geometries.

entry.title: VarioPath: Workload-Aware All-to-All Communication for PCIe GPU Clusters
entry.summary: VarioPath: Workload-Aware All-to-All Communication for PCIe GPU Clusters arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper presents VarioPath, a scheduling framework for AlltoAllv communication on PCIe GPU systems, which is important for distributed mixture-of-experts model inference. It pairs an offline topology-aware analyzer with an online demand-aware scheduler to handle link contention and skewed, changing traffic. On four platforms with up to 256 GPUs, the authors report average AlltoAllv speedups of 5.88x over FAST and 1.72x over DeepEP. End-to-end, Qwen3 inference latency falls by up to 27.2% and Wan2.1 generation latency by 6.1%.

entry.title: HyDra: a scalable system that fixes load imbalance in dynamic context parallelism for long-context training
entry.summary: HyDra: Demystifying and Taming Dynamic Context Parallelism at Production Scale arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper studies dynamic context parallelism (DCP) for long-context model training, where Megatron-Core DCP sizes parallelism to fit memory, causing uneven computation across ranks. In a production 256K-context job on over 11K GPUs, per-rank microbatch times differed by up to 5x. The authors present HyDra, a load-driven scheduler combined with a nested Ulysses-in-ring CP engine. On a 2,048-GPU production job, HyDra reduced the pipeline bubble from 36% to 14% and improved throughput by 1.10 to 1.43x over Mcore DCP.

entry.title: RIS-assisted multiuser NOMA networks robust to hardware impairments and imperfect channel information
entry.summary: RIS-Assisted Multiuser NOMA Networks With Imperfect CSI Under Transceiver Hardware Impairments arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies RIS-assisted single-beam and multi-beam NOMA networks affected by transceiver hardware impairments and imperfect channel state information. The authors propose a robust scheme that minimizes base station transmit power while meeting users' target rates, solved with Bernstein-type inequality and semi-definite relaxation. Numerical results show the proposed scheme outperforms a non-robust RIS-assisted NOMA scheme that ignores these impairments, and multi-beam NOMA achieves higher beam gain than single-beam NOMA.

entry.title: Offline-designed variances for parallel perturbed successive cancellation decoding of polar codes
entry.summary: Parallel Successive Cancellation Perturbation-Enhanced Decoding of Polar Codes via Offline Variance Design arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper proposes OVD-PSCP, a parallel successive cancellation perturbation-enhanced decoder for short and medium polar codes, in which the perturbation variances are chosen offline before decoding. Because all branches, including the original SC branch, can start simultaneously, the method avoids the extra latency of schemes that generate perturbations from earlier decoding outcomes. Simulations for rate-1/2 polar codes of lengths 64 to 512 show lower block error rates than conventional SCP with the same number of perturbation branches, with larger gains for shorter codes and more branches.

entry.title: Repairing DAG workflow schedules after link disruptions
entry.summary: Schedule Repair for DAG Workflows under Link Disruptions arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper studies how to repair schedules for DAG workflows in networked IoT systems when link disruptions invalidate parts of them. It compares four repair scopes: waiting out the disruption, rerouting, rescheduling only affected tasks, and rescheduling all pending tasks globally, each measured against an oracle and charged a latency cost. Across 100 workload instances and different disruption processes, no single scope wins, and the authors conclude the repair scope should adapt to the disruption process and repair cost.

entry.title: Provably efficient, manipulation-resistant linear regression: tight bounds
entry.summary: Tight Efficiency Guarantees for Strategyproof Linear Regression arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 The paper studies the trade-off between prediction accuracy and incentive compatibility in linear regression, where agents privately report labels and prefer predictions close to their true values. The authors give a deterministic group-strategyproof mechanism achieving a (d+1)-approximation to the least-squares optimum and show this is optimal even among universally strategyproof randomized mechanisms, answering an open question from Chen et al. (EC 2018). Under strategyproofness in expectation, squared individual loss keeps the factor d+1, while absolute individual loss achieves the tight ratio 2-1/(⌈d/2⌉+1). ★★★★★ Notable: Resolves an open question of Chen et al. with tight approximation ratios and optimality proofs for strategyproof linear regression mechanisms.

entry.title: Performance vs Portability in HPC: Why Benchmark Before Running
entry.summary: Performance vs Portability in Heterogeneous HPC Environments: Why Pre-execution Benchmarking is Required arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper compares running quantum chemistry software in Podman containers against running it directly on HPC systems, using precompiled executables with CPU-optimized builds across multiple compute nodes and no extra network tuning. The results show that performance depends on how the software was compiled, startup overhead, and execution configuration. Container preparation can dominate short tasks, while long calculations need progress monitoring. The authors conclude that workload-specific benchmarking and user-level monitoring are important when deploying scientific applications in containers on HPC systems.

entry.title: Soft-Output GRAND-Aided Macrosymbol: A Joint Detection and Decoding Method for NOMA
entry.summary: Soft-Output GRAND-Aided Macrosymbol arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 This paper extends GRAND-AM, a coding-based joint multiuser detection and error correction method for NOMA systems, into a soft-output version called SOGRAND-AM. It produces calibrated bitwise a posteriori error probabilities and works with soft-decision outer forward error correction decoders. According to the paper, SOGRAND-AM achieves about a 2 dB bit error rate improvement at the outer soft-input decoder's output compared with hard-input GRAND-AM.

entry.title: Proof of the Braun-Etzion-Vardy bound for binary subspace codes
entry.summary: A proof of the Braun-Etzion-Vardy bound for binary subspace codes arXiv · Sep 28, 2026 Linear subspace codes are codes defined within projective spaces. Braun, Etzion and Vardy (2013) conjectured that a linear subspace code in projective space has at most 2^n codewords. This paper resolves that conjecture. It uses a novel character-theoretic argument and the proof is self-contained. ★★★★★ Notable: Resolves an open conjecture via a novel character-theoretic argument with a complete, self-contained proof.

entry.title: A continuous projection converse and weighted construction for uniquely decodable code pairs
entry.summary: A Continuous Projection Converse and a Weighted Construction for Uniquely Decodable Code Pairs arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 This paper studies the maximum sum rate of uniquely decodable code pairs. A weighted refinement of a complement-gluing construction gives an explicit code of length 672 with sum rate above 1.318639029203. An iterated projection argument, combined with a conditional entropy estimate and a justified continuous limit, yields an upper bound of 1.480063425539.

entry.title: Randomized allocations balancing ex-ante and ex-post fairness under subadditive valuations
entry.summary: On best of both worlds allocations with subadditive valuations arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 This paper studies allocating indivisible goods to agents with equal entitlements and subadditive valuations. The authors give a transformation that turns any algorithm producing ρ-MMS allocations into a randomized algorithm that is ρ-MMS ex-post and η-MES ex-ante. They prove η is at least min[ρ/(2+ρ), 1/4] and apply the transformation to existing algorithms for subadditive and XOS valuations.

entry.title: Adaptive client clustering and coordination for managing federated learning workflows at the edge
entry.summary: Adaptive Client Clustering and Coordination for Federated Learning Workflow Management in Edge Networks arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 This paper proposes A-CoDa, a framework for managing dependent federated learning workflows in edge networks.
