It groups clients by label-distribution divergence and selects participants using FedMIX, which ranks clients by loss, latency, and uncertainty. A dependency-aware DAG scheduler orchestrates layer-wise task execution. Experiments on handwriting, wearable-sensing, product-image, and medical-imaging tasks show reduced end-to-end completion time while maintaining competitive accuracy.

entry.title: Gaps and Augmentations in Bayesian Scheduling
entry.summary: Gaps and Augmentations in Bayesian Scheduling arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 This paper studies how prior information, Bayesian incentive compatibility, randomization, and machine-side resource augmentation affect the approximation barrier for makespan scheduling on unrelated machines. It proves an asymptotic 4/3 lower bound for randomized BIC mechanisms with two machines and shows randomized BIC mechanisms can beat deterministic ones, with an integrality gap of 8/7. It also shows that under a spreading condition on job assignments, O(m/ε) sampled layers let the truthful MinWork mechanism reach a 1+ε approximation.

entry.title: Toward system-of-systems integration for composable cloud, HPC, and edge AI platforms
entry.summary: Toward System-of-Systems Integration for Composable Cloud-HPC-Edge AI Platforms arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 This paper argues that modern AI platforms combining cloud, HPC, cloud-native, and edge stacks can be viewed as systems of systems, where each constituent keeps its own control and failure semantics. It proposes composable integration based on interfaces, contracts, and operational evidence, without requiring a single orchestration stack. The authors present a peer constituent-system view, a boundary test, a shared responsibility model, seven integration surfaces, and a cross-system workflow example. They close with evidence classes and research questions for evaluating interoperability, governance, observability, and fault containment.

entry.title: Geometry-aware multi-UAV full-duplex communication system and field experiment
entry.summary: Geometry-Aware Multi-UAV Full-Duplex Communication: System Design and Experiment arXiv · Sep 27, 2026 This paper presents a multi-UAV in-band full-duplex communication system that uses high-gain directional antennas and separated uplink and downlink channels. It turns self-interference into controllable co-channel interference between UAVs, avoiding energy-intensive self-interference cancelers on the UAVs. The authors derive a geometry-aware interference model and define a reliable operating region in 3D airspace where the SINR requirement is met. Field trials with two UAVs and a ground station show downlink capacity that exceeds conventional TDD and approaches ideal full-duplex in most of the airspace.

entry.title: Coded Computing for Dynamic Systems Using Cartesian Products
entry.summary: Coded Computing for Dynamic System via Cartesian Products arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 Coded distributed computing reduces Shuffle communication bottlenecks through coded multicast, but existing schemes assume a fixed set of workers and do not adapt to arrivals and disconnections. This paper proposes a dynamic scheme that keeps surviving workers' caches and Reduce assignments while using storage from newly arriving clusters. File placement uses Cartesian products of cluster-wise placement delivery arrays, and a greedy algorithm reassigns abandoned Reduce functions. The authors derive the exact communication load for arbitrary feasible disconnections and show, under one-shot communication and uncoded placement, that the scheme is within a factor of two of the lower bound when new clusters arrive without disconnections, and within a factor of four otherwise.

entry.title: Codes that fix two deletions using only three extra symbols over large alphabets
entry.summary: Systematic Codes Correcting Two Deletions with Three Redundant Symbols over Large Alphabets arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper builds systematic codes over polynomial-size alphabets that correct two deletions using three redundant symbols, with polynomial-time encoding and decoding. A cardinality bound by Liu and Xing shows three redundant symbols are necessary, so the construction is optimal in this respect. The authors also show existence of such codes over alphabets of size O(n^4) and give a polynomial-time construction for a single burst of two adjacent deletions.

entry.title: Four New Binary Codes Correcting Single Errors
entry.summary: Four New Single-Error-Correcting Binary Codes arXiv · Oct 17, 2026 The paper constructs four binary codes: a (16, 3072, 3) code, a (17, 6144, 3) code, an (18, 12288, 3) code, and a (19, 24576, 3) code. These yield four new lower bounds on A(n,3) for n = 16 to 19. Each code is a union of cosets of a linear code, and the constructions were found by a computer search using a tabu search algorithm.

entry.title: Robustness in Mechanism Design: A Worst-Case Review of Auction and Exchange Mechanisms
entry.summary: Robustness in Mechanism Design arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This article reviews robust design and analysis of auctions, using the computer science paradigm that measures robustness by the worst-case ratio, over environments, between a robust auction's performance and an optimal auction's. It covers robust analysis of the first-price auction for welfare, prior-robust auction design for revenue, and prior-robust exchange mechanism design for gains from trade. It also shows that the revelation principle can lose performance in robust design, quantified by the revelation gap.

entry.title: From Pilots to Production: Lessons on Multi-Site Federated AI for Science
entry.summary: From Pilots to Production: Lessons in Cross-Institutional Federated Training and Artificial Intelligence for Science arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 Many valuable scientific datasets cannot be centralized due to proprietary, export-control, classification, or data-sovereignty limits, so the model must move to the data. The paper synthesizes lessons from U.S. Department of Energy national laboratories, industry deployments, and open-source efforts on moving federated AI from pilots to production. It organizes these lessons around a five-domain readiness frame covering data architecture, privacy and security, trust and verification, governance, and operations. It also identifies open problems such as asynchronous federation, leakage auditing, verification standards, and harmonized data contracts.

entry.title: Recovery sets and service rates of codes built by Plotkin-type construction
entry.summary: Recovery Set Structures and Service Rates of Codes Obtained by the Plotkin-type Construction arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper studies service rate regions for binary codes used in distributed storage, where data can be recovered from several disjoint server groups. It shows how recovery sets of a Plotkin-type code arise from those of its underlying code, and uses recovery hypergraphs to bound service rates. The results are applied to first-order binary Reed-Muller codes, showing that service rates for R(1,m) can be derived recursively from the generator matrix of R(1,2).

entry.title: Practical codes for computing Boolean functions over channels for decision tasks
entry.summary: Task-Oriented Boolean Function Computation: Practical Code Constructions arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 The paper proposes a practical Reed-Solomon-based code construction for Boolean function computation, where a receiver determines a function value unknown to the transmitter. For noiseless binary channels, it derives finite-blocklength worst-case error bounds and characterizes rate-reliability tradeoffs across function families. The construction is extended to noisy channels by concatenation with a conventional channel code, and numerical results report SNR coding gains over conventional transmission for specific tasks.

entry.title: The Cost of Truthfulness in Fair Cloud Resource Sharing
entry.summary: The Price of Strategyproofness in Fair Multi-Resource Allocation for Cloud Computing arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper studies how to fairly and truthfully divide several divisible resources among users with Leontief preferences, a setting motivated by cloud computing. It introduces a parametric mechanism family (ASF) and a Corrected Resource Balancing (CRB) mechanism, measuring efficiency with the fair-ratio benchmark. For two resources, CRB achieves fair-ratio at most 1+1/n, which is asymptotically optimal; for three or more resources, deterministic mechanisms satisfying sharing incentive and strategy-proofness have fair-ratio exactly m. ★★★★ Notable: Introduces ASF and CRB mechanisms, improving the two-resource fair-ratio from 1.268 to 1+Θ(1/n) with matching lower bounds, rigorously proven.

entry.title: Certified Splitting: Checking Safe Cut Points for Maximal-Munch Tokenization
entry.summary: Certified Splitting: Decidability and Anchor Supply for Maximal-Munch Tokenization arXiv · Oct 5, 2026 This paper studies how to certify byte windows in maximal-munch tokenization, where a window is a certified anchor if, in any fully tokenizable input containing it, the token covering its last byte starts at the window's origin. It gives an online method for literal vocabularies and an offline verifier for arbitrary regular token sets. The authors prove that cutting inputs at certified anchors and scanning chunks independently reproduces sequential segmentation, and they supply executable checks and measurements from shipped programs. ★★★★ Notable: Offers decidable anchor certification with theorems on splitting, edits, and differential auditing; executable checks and measured chunked scanning support claims, useful for tokenization.

entry.title: Large-scale analysis of IO500 benchmark results for storage performance
entry.summary: Repository-Scale Performance Characterization of the IO500 Benchmark arXiv · Oct 5, 2026 This paper analyzes 294 post-reset IO500 submissions from 116 sites between 2019 and 2025 to study storage performance. It examines how individual benchmark phases relate to composite rankings. Phases measuring similar I/O behavior are strongly correlated, while bandwidth and metadata performance show weaker, scale-dependent relationships. Temporal and log-level analysis reveals information not visible in aggregate scores.

entry.title: Fitting Fluid Antenna Channels with Extreme Value Distributions for Accurate Outage Evaluation
entry.summary: A FAS Channel Fitting Strategy Using Extreme Value Distributions for Accurate Outage Performance Evaluation arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper proposes a channel fitting strategy for single-antenna fluid antenna systems (FAS) that focuses on accurately evaluating outage probability (OP). It introduces a combined extreme value distribution (CEVD), using a generalized Pareto distribution for the left tail and a generalized extreme value distribution for global behavior. A modified mean-square-error criterion with logarithmic-domain errors and uniform sampling on the log CDF is developed to emphasize tail accuracy. Simulations show improved OP evaluation accuracy in the ultra-low-OP regime.

entry.title: Near-optimal coded caching that keeps both files and user demands private
entry.summary: Order-Optimal Coded Caching With File and Demand Privacy arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper studies coded caching where both file contents and user requests stay private: each user gets only its requested file and learns nothing about other files or other users' requests. The authors propose a scheme whose worst-case delivery rate is at most 9/2 times optimal, for all user and file counts and feasible cache sizes. They also derive lower bounds on delivery rate and exact results at minimal memory and unit delivery rate. ★★★★ Notable: Gives near-optimal coded caching under joint file and demand privacy, with entropy-based lower bounds matching up to constants, a substantial theoretical advance.

entry.title: SyclKittens: A Tile Programming Model for Intel GPU Programmers and Coding Agents
entry.summary: SyclKittens: A Tile Programming Model for Programmers and Coding Agents on Intel GPUs arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 The paper presents SyclKittens, a hardware-aware tile programming model for Intel GPUs that encodes known-good methods such as matrix-engine operand layouts, L1 prefetching, and fabric communication. Under the same agent and budget, an agent using SyclKittens reaches 82.1% of Intel's oneDNN library on a GEMM kernel, compared with 57.5% using raw SYCL. The resulting kernel suite reaches about 96% of oneDNN in geometric mean across GEMM shapes and runs Llama-3.1-8B inference 1.59x faster than torch.compile on one GPU. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes a hardware-aware tile model encoding known methods, validated by controlled GEMM and Llama-3.1-8B inference comparisons against oneDNN and oneCCL.

entry.title: One-shot beam tracking for stacked metasurface-assisted satellite broadcasting
entry.summary: One-Shot Beam Tracking for Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces-Assisted LEO Broadcasting arXiv · Oct 5, 2026 This paper proposes a physics-informed one-shot beam tracking method for low-Earth-orbit satellite links assisted by a multilayer stacked intelligent metasurface. It predicts signal-quality changes from orbital motion and maps them to the metasurface phase settings through an analytical Jacobian, requiring only a single regularized correction. Numerical results show it keeps about 92% to 94% of the rate of iterative reoptimization while running hundreds of times faster.

entry.title: Optimistic reliable broadcast with three-step latency
entry.summary: Optimistic Reliable Broadcast in Three Steps arXiv · Oct 5, 2026 This paper studies latency tradeoffs in signature-free asynchronous reliable broadcast that allow optimistic two-step delivery. The authors present two constructions that improve optimistic, honest-broadcaster, and totality delay bounds within specific ranges of parties and faults. They also prove a matching lower bound showing that, at maximal optimism, totality delay is at least three steps. The results indicate that maximal optimism costs one extra totality step compared with Bracha's protocol without increasing good-case latency. ★★★★★ Notable: Gives new signature-free reliable broadcast constructions with optimistic two-step delivery and a matching lower bound proof, a clear theoretical improvement.

entry.title: Modulation and Integration in a Local Processor Receiving Two Input Sources
entry.summary: Modulation and Integration in a local processor having input from two distinct sources arXiv · Oct 5, 2026 This paper uses partial information decomposition to analyse how a local processor that receives two integrated input streams transmits information. The authors revise earlier conditions for contextual modulation and add a condition for signal integration, computing exact information-theoretic results with the Ibroja method. They test these conditions across several activation functions and apply them to noisy simulation data from a model layer 5b pyramidal cell, reporting evidence of basal-apical modulation and integration.

entry.title: A simple algorithm that beats the 1/3 approximation barrier for Nash equilibria in two-player games
entry.summary: A Simple Algorithm Breaking the 1/3 Barrier for Approximate Nash Equilibria in Bimatrix Games arXiv · Oct 5, 2026 Computing Nash equilibria in bimatrix games is PPAD-complete, and this paper studies the strongest approximation guarantee achievable in polynomial time. The authors propose a simple, symmetric, deterministic polynomial-time algorithm with no tunable hyperparameters, achieving an approximation of about 0.30954+δ and breaking the long-standing 1/3 barrier. The method extends the optimization framework of Tsaknakis and Spirakis with building blocks from the authors' work on strategy mixing and automated approximation analysis. ★★★★★ Notable: Breaks the long-standing 1/3 barrier for approximate Nash equilibria with a new algorithmic structure and conceptual explanation.

entry.title: Row-weight limits on redundant checks for peeling decoding of random LDPC codes
entry.summary: Limits of Weight-Bounded Redundant Checks for Peeling Decoding of Random Regular LDPC Codes arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 The paper studies peeling decoding on the binary erasure channel when redundant parity checks can be added freely but each check has a bounded row weight. For random simple binary regular LDPC codes, it considers the parity-check matrix formed by all nonzero dual codewords up to a given weight. Within an explicit logarithmic row-weight range, this full family of redundant checks has the same asymptotic normalized-residual threshold as peeling with the original LDPC matrix. ★★★★ Notable: Proves that all low-weight redundant checks preserve the asymptotic peeling threshold of random regular LDPC codes in a logarithmic weight range, establishing a row-weight limitation with rigorous the

entry.title: Tighter Upper Bound on the Ingleton Score for Four Random Variables
entry.summary: Improved Bounds on the Ingleton Score of Four Random Variables arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper studies four finite discrete random variables and shows that the negative Ingleton expression divided by joint entropy is at most 19/124 (about 0.15323). This improves the previously reported bound of 3/19 by 11/2356. The proof uses a copy program with four copy steps and six auxiliary variables, verified by exact rational linear-programming certificates. The authors also show that two published inequalities imply the bound 5/32.

entry.title: Secure multi-access coded caching via a lifting transformation
entry.summary: Secure Multi-Access Coded Caching: A Lifting Approach arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 The paper builds secure cyclic multi-access coded caching schemes by re-encoding the caches of a secure single-access scheme while reusing its multicast message. Each user reads L consecutive shared caches, recovers its requested file, and learns nothing about other files. Deterministic Pascal-window and randomized complement-dual encoders are given, attaining exact minimum per-block storage over a suitable finite field. The resulting memory-rate family has approximation guarantees against converse bounds, and the L=K-1 tradeoff is proved exactly.

entry.title: HiNa-MoE: Fast, Non-Intrusive MoE Inference on CPUs with Matrix Engines
entry.summary: HiNa-MoE: High-Performance, Non-Intrusive MoE Inference on CPUs with Matrix Engines arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper presents HiNa-MoE, an operator library that speeds up Mixture-of-Experts model inference on Intel AMX-equipped CPUs. It keeps expert weights in standard layouts, uses a simple page-interleaved policy for NUMA-aware work partitioning, and converts decode-phase matrix-vector operations into small matrix-matrix operations. The authors report speedups of up to 3.37x for FFN kernels and up to 2.09x for end-to-end inference over baselines, and state that it works plug-and-play with existing frameworks.

entry.title: CommuteProp: Decoupled Training for Communication-Bound Split LLM Fine-Tuning
entry.summary: CommuteProp: Decoupled Training for Communication Bound Split LLM Fine-Tuning arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper addresses inefficiency in privacy-preserving split-learning fine-tuning of large language models, where clients sit idle waiting for server-side gradients. It proposes CommuteProp, an asynchronous algorithm that splits training into two concurrent phases, a cross-block forward-backward pass and an in-block weight update, so computation overlaps with communication. The authors provide asynchronous error and convergence analysis and derive an NS preconditioner to reduce staleness-induced noise. Experiments report substantial throughput gains with accuracy comparable to synchronous methods, and the method can be plugged into existing privacy-enhancement techniques.

entry.title: Secure device-to-device coded caching with limited-radius connections using lifting
entry.summary: Secure D2D Coded Caching under Radius-Limited Connectivity via Lifting arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper studies secure coded caching in a device-to-device network where users on a cycle can only communicate with nearby users within a fixed radius. Each user must generate delivery signals from its cache and recover its requested file without learning any other file. The authors construct such schemes using an outer secret-sharing code and a secure local caching scheme, and they prove information-theoretic secrecy along with converse bounds on peak sum load. Within certain memory ranges, the schemes achieve optimal load or a constant-factor approximation.

entry.title: You Only Convert Twice: Ozaki Scheme II for Repeated Tensor Mode Products
entry.summary: You Only Convert Twice: Ozaki Scheme II for Chained Tensor Mode Products arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper proposes OzII-RescaleBE, which keeps intermediate tensors in residue form during chained tensor mode products in Ozaki scheme II. Inputs are converted to residues only once at the start and reconstructed only at the end, with an implementation on INT8 Tensor Cores using CuTe DSL. Across three datasets and chain depths 3 to 7, normwise relative errors stay near 1e-16 to 1e-15, but rise to about 1e-13 at depth 8. Throughput and memory use are compared against two GEMMul8 baselines, with gains at smaller mode sizes and a slight deficit at size 256.

entry.title: Optimal colorings in unweighted Max-k-Cut games can still be unstable to group deviations
entry.summary: Social Optimality Does Not Imply Coalitional Stability in Unweighted Max-k-Cut Games arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper studies Max-k-Cut games on unweighted graphs, where optimal colorings maximize social welfare. The authors disprove a conjecture by showing that for every k≥3 there is a finite, simple, connected graph with an optimal coloring that is not a strong equilibrium. A coalition can profitably deviate to another optimal coloring, benefiting all its members while outside players lose and social welfare is unchanged. The paper also gives an exact identity linking coalition gains, cut changes and internal conflicts, and bounds monochromatic edges remaining after strong deviations from general Nash equilibria.

entry.title: Scalable distortion-aware clustering for fronthaul-limited cell-free MIMO networks
entry.summary: Scalable Distortion-Aware Clustering for Fronthaul-Limited Cell-Free MIMO Networks arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper studies how to group access points in uplink cell-free MIMO networks with fronthaul limits, using maximum ratio combining. The optimization depends only on large-scale fading coefficients, and asymptotic analysis gives deterministic equivalent expressions for average network sum rate that account for quantization distortion. The authors exploit the structure of the resulting quadratic-over-linear objective to develop a polynomial-time scheme that reaches the global optimum. Numerical results show gains over improved existing methods and competitive performance against an exhaustive-search global optimum based on small-scale fading.

entry.title: Formalizing Microwave Analog Computing in Lean
entry.summary: Toward a Lean Formalization of Analog Computing with Microwaves arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper takes a first step toward formalizing microwave analog computing in Lean, a proof assistant. Microwave signals can perform linear transformations directly as they propagate through a network. The authors formalize components such as hybrid couplers and phase shifters, their series and parallel connections, and the networks they form. They formally prove a necessary and sufficient condition for the transformations these networks can compute, and that the discrete Fourier transform of any power-of-two size is implementable. All proofs are checked by the Lean kernel, and the code is publicly available.

entry.title: A unified framework linking sensing, computation, and communication in over-the-air federated learning
entry.summary: Learning OTA: A Unified Framework for Edge Sensing, Computation, and Communication arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper addresses the fact that federated learning training data must first be collected by heterogeneous edge sensors, and that collection quality and cost affect learning performance. It models sensing noise, energy consumption, latency, and over-the-air aggregation distortion in an OTA federated learning system, and derives a non-convex convergence bound. Based on this, the authors formulate a per-round optimization balancing energy, latency, and learning quality, solved with an alternating procedure. Numerical experiments show the benefit of jointly optimizing sensing, computation, and communication decisions.

entry.title: Fluid antenna secure channel-driven constellation: a physical-layer security method for hiding data in channel points
entry.summary: Fluid Antenna Secure Channel-driven Constellation (FASCC): a Physical Layer Security approach arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper proposes the FASCC framework for downlink communication, where information is carried by constellation points formed through fluid antenna port selection and phase adaptation. Two complementary schemes are developed depending on whether the eavesdropper's channel state information is available. Numerical results show significant secrecy gains in bit error rate and mutual-information secrecy, even when the eavesdropper is much closer to the base station than the legitimate user.

entry.title: Approximate feedback Nash equilibria in constrained games via model predictive control with a provable error bound
entry.summary: Approximate Feedback Nash Equilibria in Constrained Differential Games via Model Predictive Control with Upper Bound Guarantees arXiv · Oct 4, 2026 This paper proposes a model predictive control method that approximates feedback Nash equilibrium trajectories in differential games by repeatedly solving finite-horizon open-loop games. An auxiliary-game formulation selects prediction horizons and terminal costs, and hard constraints are incorporated through a constrained open-loop game. For the unconstrained case, the authors derive an analytic upper bound on the state-trajectory deviation from the true equilibrium, and they compare the method numerically with baseline approaches.

entry.title: Joint source-channel coding of Gaussian sources over block erasure channels, with nonasymptotic bounds and channel-uniform normal approximations
entry.summary: Joint Source-Channel Coding of Gaussian Sources over Block Erasure Channels: Nonasymptotic Bounds and Channel-Uniform Normal Approximations arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 The paper studies lossy transmission of a Gaussian memoryless source over memoryless, possibly nonstationary block erasure channels at finite blocklength, under an excess mean-squared distortion criterion. It derives computable nonasymptotic achievability and converse bounds and establishes matching third-order, channel-uniform normal approximations. Numerical evaluations compare these joint source-channel coding bounds and their common approximation with an optimized symmetrized separate source-channel coding benchmark.

entry.title: Plotkin-Type Bounds for Function-Correcting Codes on Monomial Maps
entry.summary: Plotkin-type Bound on Function-Correcting Codes for Monomial Mappings arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper studies function-correcting codes (FCCs), which give the receiver stronger protection for a function of the message than for the message itself. For arbitrary functions over finite fields under the Hamming metric, the authors derive a generalised Plotkin-type bound on FCC redundancy that reduces to the classical Plotkin bound for ordinary error-correcting codes. Explicit bounds are also obtained for linear functions, Hamming-weight functions, and Hamming-weight threshold functions. The paper further derives an explicit redundancy bound for monomial mappings f(x)=x^n over the field F_{q^k}.

entry.title: Resource pattern design for V2X-ISAC under communication quality constraints
entry.summary: QoS-Constrained Resource Pattern Design for V2X-ISAC Systems arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper proposes a method for selecting sensing resource patterns in vehicle-to-everything integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, considering both communication reliability and sensing performance. Sensing is based on the Fisher information matrix for joint range and velocity estimation, with a minimum packet reception ratio imposed as a QoS constraint. A greedy selection algorithm with one-swap refinement is developed to avoid exhaustive search. Simulations show improved sensing over conventional patterns while meeting the PRR requirement, with performance close to the exhaustive-search optimum.

entry.title: Timely persuasion by two opposing senders: does competition help the receiver?
entry.summary: Timely Persuasion with Opposing Senders: When Does Competition Help the Receiver? arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 Two senders with opposing preferences each send status updates about a binary continuous-time Markov chain under individual budgets. The receiver follows the reports only if doing so yields at least the long-run utility of a prior-based default estimate. The authors model the interaction as a Stackelberg game, characterize its pure-strategy equilibria in closed form, and compare receiver utility with a single sender and with a receiver-optimal reporting benchmark.

entry.title: Recovering a hidden linear system and its starting states from partial observations.
entry.summary: Identification and Recovery of Linear Dynamics from Partial Trajectories arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper studies how to jointly recover an unknown system matrix A and a low-rank initial-state matrix X0 from observations of the state trajectories A^t X0 that cover only some coordinates. It gives necessary identifiability conditions, lower bounds on the number of observations, and a rank-based principle for generic local identifiability. When trajectories from a basis of the initial-state range are fully observed, it provides necessary and sufficient rank conditions for global recovery with explicit formulas. Numerical experiments on synthetic and real data assess performance under different sampling rates and horizons.

entry.title: Computing Equilibria in Integer Games with Shared Constraints
entry.summary: Computing Equilibria in Integer Programming Games with Shared Constraints arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 The paper presents a cutting-plane algorithm for computing pure Nash equilibria in finite integer games where deviations depend on opponents' choices due to shared constraints. Conditional equilibrium inequalities are embedded as lazy constraints in branch-and-cut to optimize over exact or approximate equilibria. Evaluated on 3,300 instances, the method finds a socially optimal equilibrium in nearly all cases and certifies nonexistence in 16.

entry.title: OACM: An Optimistic Asynchronous Communication Model for Large-Scale Spiking Neural Network Simulation
entry.summary: OACM: Optimistic Asynchronous Communication Model for Large-Scale SNN Simulation arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper proposes OACM, a communication model for simulating large-scale spiking neural networks across distributed computers. It combines optimistic hybrid simulation with rollbacks, asynchronous one-sided communication via the UNR library, and adaptive message aggregation and routing on a 2D-HyperX topology. On a high-performance computing cluster simulating a multi-area marmoset brain model with up to 174 nodes, the authors report up to 1.4x speedup over the original CORTEX simulator and over 22.6x speedup compared to NEST.

entry.title: Learning in large populations with anticipatory payoffs, combining Bregman divergence with Willems and Lyapunov methods
entry.summary: Learning in Large Populations With Anticipatory Payoffs: Bregman Meets Willems and Lyapunov arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 The paper studies evolutionary Nash equilibrium learning in large populations whose payoffs come from dynamic mechanisms. Using counterclockwise dissipativity (CCW), it shows convergence for a broad class of well-behaved learning rules that align with payoffs. It then builds rule-independent Lyapunov functions from CCW storage functions, filling the gap where earlier results gave convergence but no Lyapunov stability. For a nonlinear anticipatory mechanism, the storage function is a Bregman divergence, and the resulting Lyapunov function establishes global asymptotic stability. A congestion game with a nonlinear congestion-growth toll illustrates the results.

entry.title: BitIR: A Cross-Architecture Fault Injection Tool for Testing How Heterogeneous GPU Programs Handle Faults
entry.summary: BitIR: Cross-Architecture Fault Injection for Resilience Analysis of Heterogeneous GPU Applications arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper presents BitIR, a framework that injects single-bit faults at the LLVM IR level so the same perturbation can be compared across NVIDIA, Intel, and AMD GPUs. The authors ran large injection campaigns on the Polaris, Aurora, and Frontier supercomputers using heterogeneous benchmarks. Outcomes were sorted into masked results, silent data corruptions, and failures. The results show that identical faults behave differently across vendors, so resilience depends on the backend.

entry.title: Deterministic Stackelberg Strategies for Robotaxi Vehicle Assignment
entry.summary: Deterministic Stackelberg Strategies in Robotaxi Assignment Games arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper studies competition between two robotaxi platforms, where an incumbent must dispatch its fleet to limit riders poached by a reactive entrant. The authors model this as a zero-sum assignment game and give an exact integer linear program, plus a polynomial-time approximation algorithm. They prove that computing or approximating the optimal payoff is hard in general, and provide an exact dynamic programming method for riders and vehicles on a line. Experiments on real ride-hailing data show the LP-based method performs well in practice, and simple heuristics are competitive.

entry.title: SIC-based multi-way communication using reconfigurable intelligent surfaces
entry.summary: RIS Aided Multi-Way Communication Systems based on SIC Decoding Techniques arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper studies multi-way communication systems aided by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) using QPSK, where multiple users exchange information by exploiting the RIS's full-duplex capability. Three successive interference cancellation (SIC) ordering methods are compared by bit error rate through Monte-Carlo simulations, and an extension to RIS elements with phase-dependent amplitudes is considered. Results show that with few RIS elements, SIC ordered by increasing mean square error performs best, while with more elements, the optimization-based ordering performs best.

entry.title: A tighter upper bound on the size of recovering pairs
entry.summary: An Improved Upper Bound for Recovering Pairs arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 The paper proves that for any recovering pair of nonempty families of subsets of an n-element set, the product of the family sizes is at most (2.23949)^n. Previously, combining a result of Mond, Souza and Versteegen with the Fang-Huang bound gave (2.2499)^n. The proof combines two entropy inequalities through a convex combination. ★★★★ Notable: Combines two entropy inequalities via convex combination to improve the exponential bound for recovering pairs from 2.2499^n to 2.23949^n.

entry.title: Multiple Access in Pinching-Antenna Systems: Survey and Impairment Evaluation
entry.summary: Multiple Access in Pinching-Antenna Systems: A Survey, Impairment Analysis, and Evaluation arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper surveys multiple access techniques for pinching-antenna systems, which attach dielectric pinches to a waveguide to create nearby line-of-sight radiation points. It organizes fifty-six works into a unified taxonomy by spatial degrees of freedom, showing users on one waveguide can be separated only by time, frequency, power, or guided mode. The authors identify impairments that disrupt this separation and evaluate time, frequency, power, and space-domain access under identical models, finding the degradation depends on the method.

entry.title: Fast demodulation for lattice-based coset codes (quantize-walk method)
entry.summary: Efficient Demodulation for Coset Codes on Lattices arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper addresses the high complexity of soft demodulation for lattice constellations by proposing fast quantize-walk demodulation (FQWD) for multilevel coset codes. The method uses radial projections onto the Voronoi cells of the D4 and E8 lattices to reduce complexity from O(d2^{sd}) to O(sd2^d). Experiments show only negligible block error rate loss relative to maximum likelihood demodulation under AWGN.

entry.title: Mechanism design for choosing a bridge location when agents have optional facility preferences
entry.summary: Mechanism Design for Bridge Location with Optional Preferences arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 The paper studies a bridge location problem in which two separated regions each have one prelocated facility, and each agent selects a nonempty subset of facilities she cares about. Costs are defined as the maximum, sum, or minimum distance to those facilities. The authors design deterministic strategyproof mechanisms that choose the bridge location and approximately minimize either social cost or maximum cost. They report optimal mechanisms and approximation ratios for several variants, along with lower bounds.

entry.title: Non-isomorphic graphs have distinct vertex-Ramsey classes
entry.summary: Non-isomorphic graphs have distinct vertex-Ramsey classes arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper studies the k-colour vertex Ramsey class of a graph H, the set of graphs G where any k-colouring of vertices yields a monochromatic induced copy of H. The authors prove that, for any k, non-isomorphic graphs have distinct Ramsey classes.

entry.title: Single-sample prophet inequalities via reduction from combinatorial to single-item
entry.summary: Single-Sample Prophet Inequalities: A Combinatorial to Single-Item Reduction arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper studies single-sample prophet inequalities for online combinatorial allocation, where items arrive sequentially and must be allocated. The authors give a general reduction that converts combinatorial problems into single-item prophet inequalities, using a free-disposal value to separate buyer and item constraints. The framework yields competitive ratios for XOS valuations in the single-sample and k-sample settings, and extends to divisible resources with capped-XOS valuations.

entry.title: OpenMP Meta-Lowering: A Declarative Way to Generate Parallel Code Portably
entry.summary: OpenMP Meta-Lowering: A Declarative Approach to Performance Portable Parallel Code Generation arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper presents a modular approach to parallel code generation built on MLIR, in which a domain-specific language specifies how OpenMP constructs are lowered for each target. The authors call this OpenMP meta-lowering. On PolyBench/C-OMP, it matches state-of-the-art toolchains with under 0.7% code-size overhead. The OpenMP subset is expressed in about 32% fewer lines than Clang's lowering code and about 76% fewer than GCC's, and new runtimes need only a few specification lines.

entry.title: Code distances of matrix rank-metric codes under Add-and-Remove transformations: how subcode distances change when a code is modified by removing and adding subspaces.
entry.summary: Code distances of matrix rank-metric codes under Add-and-Remove transformations arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 The paper studies how subcode distances of matrix rank-metric codes change under the Add-and-Remove construction, which keeps a subcode of codimension ℓs and adds a space of dimension ℓa. It gives inequalities between the subcode distances of the original and new codes for arbitrary matrix codes, and shows Delsarte duality interchanges ℓs and ℓa. For matrix Gabidulin codes it gives explicit behavior of subcode distances and expresses the new code's minimum distance via rank distance between the added space and the common subcode, with relevance to the MIRANDA signature scheme.

entry.title: Training one LLM across three supercomputers in two continents
entry.summary: Cross-Facility LLM Pre-training on HPC: Elastic Aggregation, Data Leasing, and Queue-Aware Placement arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper presents a system that pools compute allocations from three supercomputers (Snellius, LUMI, and Frontier), located up to 7,400 km apart, to pre-train a single language model. It combines elastic two-loop training, a heartbeat-backed data-leasing protocol that prevents samples from being duplicated or lost, and queue-aware job placement. Training Qwen3-0.6B on C4, the three-site run reached a held-out perplexity of 34.7, compared with 28.2 for a centralised baseline. ★★★★ Notable: Combines elastic cross-site training, data leasing, and queue-aware placement, validated on three supercomputers, though comparisons and scale are limited.

entry.title: RailWave: adaptive scheduling that speeds up data transfers between expert GPUs in large AI models
entry.summary: RailWave: Adaptive Spatial and Temporal Scheduling for Expert-Parallel Communication arXiv · Oct 3, 2026 This paper addresses slow, uneven data exchange (All-to-All communication) in Mixture-of-Experts AI models. It presents RailWave, a communication layer built on DeepEP that redistributes traffic across network Rails and limits concurrent senders per receiver. On communication workloads from the 106B GLM-4.5-Air model, it reports speedups of up to 5.84x on H800 and 4.36x on H20 compared with Native.

entry.title: Error-correcting codes with high girth built from higher-degree permutation polynomials
entry.summary: Low-Density Parity-Check Codes of High Girth from Permutation Polynomials arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper studies quasi-cyclic LDPC codes, whose girth and minimum distance are limited by the commutativity of their circulant permutation matrices. The authors build protograph-based codes from higher-degree permutation polynomials, focusing on a family of non-commuting binomial permutation polynomials. Simulations show better decoding performance than constructions based on affine permutation polynomials.

entry.title: Randomization Outperforms Deterministic Adaptive Parallel Sampling
entry.summary: Randomization Beyond Deterministic Adaptivity in Parallel Sampling arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 The paper studies parallel samplers that reveal each coordinate once and draw each batch independently from exact conditional marginals, under a three-round cap. For an explicit binary family, it shows randomization beats every deterministic adaptive policy: the best deterministic forward KL divergence grows linearly with dimension, while a uniform mixture of four fixed schedules is exponentially smaller. Selecting the schedule needs only two fair random bits. A finite-sum certificate confirms this separation already at dimension 389.

entry.title: VenusRL: A Fully Disaggregated Agentic RL System with Priority Scheduling
entry.summary: VenusRL: A Fully Disaggregated Agentic RL System with Priority Scheduling and Scalable Interaction arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper presents VenusRL, a fully disaggregated reinforcement learning system for training LLM agents through multi-turn tool interactions. It targets two bottlenecks: training throughput limited by the slowest trajectories, and tool sandboxes that are over-provisioned in memory. It uses priority-aware scheduling and a memory-aware page-sharing pool to address them. According to the paper, it achieves up to 4.24x end-to-end training speedup over baselines and cuts environment cost by up to 89%.

entry.title: Analysis of how well a multi-rate version of NOMA (a radio access method that shares one channel among users by power) keeps data errors low when there are many users and different symbol speeds
entry.summary: Performance Analysis of MR-NOMA with Arbitrary Number of Users and Symbol Rates arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper analytically studies the bit error rate of downlink multi-rate NOMA over Nakagami-m fading channels for any number of users and symbol rates. It derives an exact error expression for the first detected user and closed-form approximations for the others, assuming perfect successive interference cancellation. A symbol-pattern-dependent SINR analysis explains why MR-NOMA outperforms conventional single-rate NOMA, and an average BER minimization for power allocation is solved numerically and checked by simulation.

entry.title: How prompt wording shapes LLMs' tendency to follow default options in group-decision games
entry.summary: Prompt framing governs LLM default following in collective-action arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper tests whether large language models follow default values pre-filled in an interface when making choices in two one-shot social dilemmas: a common-pool resource extraction game and a threshold public-good game. Pre-filled defaults pull choices toward the default value, but the strength of this pull varies widely with wording, default type, and action-space granularity. The authors conclude that evaluating agent behaviour without controlling the choice architecture can miss a key source of variation.

entry.title: AFORE: Reconfiguring Experts Efficiently in Attention-FFN Disaggregated MoE Serving
entry.summary: AFORE: Attention-FFN Disaggregation with Overlapped Reconfiguration of Experts arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper addresses efficient serving of Mixture-of-Experts models, where uneven expert loads can slow the feed-forward stage in attention-FFN disaggregation. The authors present AFORE, which uses the upcoming microbatch expert distribution to plan expert migrations and overlaps those migrations with computation of earlier microbatches. Evaluated on a 110B-parameter MoE model over four dynamic workloads, AFORE improves output throughput by 10.1-17.6% and reduces P95 inter-token latency by 7.1-9.5% compared with the strongest baseline.

entry.title: Closing the Prediction Gap: Completing Machine Shape to Match Real Hardware Behavior
entry.summary: Closing the Prediction Gap: Completing Machine Shape So That Predicted Time, Power, Energy, and Mapping Match What Real Hardware Does arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper completes a device-shape description used to partition work across heterogeneous, multi-institution hardware ensembles without communication. It fills in five previously unmeasured fields, including memory capacity, power draw, execution unit capability, compiler directive configuration, and memory reservation overhead, and adds a Boolean reached(d) to explain an NVIDIA fp16 power shift. The fields are measured on five devices (A100, H100, V100, MI100, Max 1550), with reservation overhead ranging from about 0.004 to 0.030 and a residual of negative 9.8 percent for the excluded Triton autotuner.

entry.title: PaNGEA: A GPU-Based Parallel Method for Finding Good Solutions in Mixed-Integer Optimization
entry.summary: PaNGEA: Parallel Node Generation and Exploration Algorithm on GPU arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper introduces PaNGEA, a primal heuristic designed to run efficiently on GPUs for mixed-integer optimization problems. It combines linear-relaxation solves with a batched local-search procedure and generates multiple restricted subproblems in parallel. On 283 MIPcc26 and MIPLIB instances, the single-node GPU version reduces the average gap integral by 8-18% compared with its CPU counterpart, and parallel exploration of multiple nodes reduces it by a further 12-19%.

entry.title: Coda: Using Admission Flexibility to Speed Up Coding-Agent Serving
entry.summary: Coda: Exploiting Admission Flexibility for Coding-Agent Serving arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 Coding agents alternate between LLM inference and tool calls, producing long sessions with reusable KV states. The paper finds two inefficiencies in shared serving systems: KV states sit across storage tiers with unequal preparation costs, and requests with different context lengths decode poorly together. It presents Coda, which uses Tiered-Aging state admission and Compatibility-Aware execution admission, plus a routing layer for multi-worker setups. Coda improves output-token and SLO-compliant throughput by 20.3% and 70.5% on average over prior systems and vLLM.

entry.title: Coverage Depth in Distributed DNA Storage: When Sampling Cuts Sequencing Cost
entry.summary: The Coverage Depth Problem in Distributed DNA Data Storage arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper studies how many DNA reads are needed to recover a full message in distributed DNA storage when strands are randomly sampled from containers. It derives exact formulas for recovery time for arbitrary linear codes and ordered partitions. The authors show MDS codes are optimal for each fixed partition and identify when distributed sampling reduces total reads rather than only parallelizing them. ★★★★ Notable: Derives exact recovery-time formulas, proves MDS codes optimal, and resolves a conjecture on simplex codes, a strong theoretical contribution for DNA storage.

entry.title: Pricing Time, Not Just Tokens: Latency-Aware Pricing Mechanisms for LLM Inference
entry.summary: Pricing Time, Not Just Tokens: Latency-Aware Mechanism Design for LLM Inference arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 The paper models LLM inference as a service market in which buyers have private willingness-to-pay, task volume, and time preference, and utility depends on both token counts and latency slack. Its main result is a separation theorem: discrete hardware tiers make buyers self-select on time preference, reducing three-dimensional screening to one-dimensional screening within each tier. The authors characterize optimal tiered mechanisms using virtual-value techniques and calibrate them to 8-GPU H100 and B200 clusters.

entry.title: PaxosLease in Relativistic Inertial Frames
entry.summary: PaxosLease in Relativistic Inertial Frames arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 The paper examines whether the PaxosLease distributed lease protocol remains safe under special relativity, where simultaneity is frame-dependent. It restates the safety property using light cones, requiring a lease expiry to lie in the causal past of any later acquisition by a different holder. The authors modify classical PaxosLease by adding a relativistic Doppler factor to its containment and quarantine rules.

entry.title: ByteSplat: Faster distributed 3D Gaussian Splatting training by cutting GPU data movement
entry.summary: ByteSplat: Efficient Distributed 3D Gaussian Splatting Training via Intra- and Inter-GPU communication reduction arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) reconstructs photorealistic scenes, but training large scenes demands much memory and computation. ByteSplat is a distributed training framework that targets two bottlenecks: repeated off-chip memory access during rasterization and inter-GPU communication of partial gradients. It fuses forward and backward rasterization into one kernel, adds hardware-aware pruning, and removes zero gradients from communication. On six datasets, it cuts intra-GPU off-chip traffic by 63.4% and backward inter-GPU communication by 65.8%, reaching up to 6.1x training speedup on eight GPUs while preserving reconstruction quality.

entry.title: Whether OFDM is optimal for aperiodic ranging signals
entry.summary: On the Optimality of OFDM for Aperiodic Ranging arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper studies the expected aperiodic autocorrelation sidelobes of random communication symbols sent through a unitary modulation matrix, for constellations such as uniform QAM and PSK. For each lag it determines the exact minimum expected sidelobe level and a unitary modulation that attains it. The full OFDM modulation attains this minimum if and only if the lag divides the block length N, and simultaneous optimality over all positive lags is shown to be impossible for N ≥ 3.

entry.title: AI-assisted GPU optimization of a variational method for few-body boson systems
entry.summary: AI-Assisted GPU optimization of the Stochastic Variational Method for Few-Body Boson System arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 The stochastic variational method is a precise approach for quantum few-body systems in fields such as nuclear and atomic physics. The authors built a parallel code for helium-4 few-body clusters, optimized for NVIDIA GH200 and AMD MI300A GPUs, with the whole code written by an AI coding agent. They introduce a secular-equation method with the Gu–Eisenstat prescription for the generalized eigenvalue problem, and tune performance by batching small matrices and optimizing memory layout. For a five-body system with 4800 basis states, the tuned code is reported to run 16.2 and 14.7 times faster than the tuned CPU version, and 168 and 153 times faster than the first CPU implementation.

entry.title: ServeTwin: A Benchmark-Validated Simulator for Exploring Distributed LLM Serving Designs
entry.summary: ServeTwin: A Benchmark-Validated Simulator for Distributed LLM Architecture Exploration arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper presents ServeTwin, a closed-loop simulator for evaluating distributed LLM serving designs without costly physical clusters. It couples specification-driven analytical timing with a stateful serving loop and can run unmodified serving benchmarks. Compared with real deployments, it reproduces a steady-state throughput-interactivity frontier with 3.6% mean error and predicts multi-turn performance with 9.9% error.

entry.title: Annotation-driven migration of CUDA programs to Tenstorrent Blackhole hardware
entry.summary: Annotation-Driven Migration of CUDA Programs to Tenstorrent Blackhole arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 The paper presents an MLIR-based compiler that migrates statically shaped affine CUDA programs to the Tenstorrent Blackhole platform, deriving data placement, inter-core communication, and tile computation. Declarative annotations let developers specify choices the source leaves open, such as where compute and data-movement operations are placed and streaming granularity. On Gaussian elimination, a five-point stencil, and symmetric rank-k update, the best configurations reach a 4.2x speedup for BF16 Gaussian and 2.1 to 2.2x for FP32 Gaussian and Jacobi, relative to the compiler's defaults. The authors note that a choice's performance effect can reverse depending on surrounding policies, precision, and loop schedule, so alternative per-core realizations should be compared rather than policies selected independently.

entry.title: Beaver: Elastic GPU Sharing for ML and Latency-Critical vRAN Workloads
entry.summary: Beaver: Elastic GPU Sharing between ML and Latency-Critical vRAN Workloads arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper presents Beaver, a system that lets a latency-critical radio network workload and a throughput-oriented machine learning workload share the same GPU. It adjusts streaming multiprocessor allocation per time slot and rewrites ML kernels to yield memory bandwidth during the radio workload's memory-intensive phases. On an H200 GPU, the authors report that the radio workload's p99.9 latency stays within its 1.5ms uplink deadline while retaining 74% of Llama-3.3-70B serving throughput.

entry.title: Existence of Two-Sided Product Expanding Codes Using Rademacher Matrices
entry.summary: Two-Sided Product Expanding Codes via Rademacher Matrices arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 The paper proves that two-sided product expanding codes exist without relying on explicit constructions of asymptotically optimal locally testable codes (c³-LTCs), unlike an earlier result by Kalachev and Panteleev. It shows that independent random linear codes over a sufficiently large prime field have constant two-sided product expansion with probability tending to one, for fixed numbers of component codes with rates bounded away from zero and one. The trade-off is that the field characteristic must grow with the block length, whereas the earlier work used extensions of F₂.

entry.title: Burning Signed Graphs: Two competing fires spread on signed graphs, aiming to burn as many vertices of one colour as possible.
entry.summary: Burning Signed Graphs arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 The paper introduces a new graph burning model in which yellow and green fires ignite vertices of a signed graph and spread along edges, with an edge's sign determining whether the fire changes colour. Each step, a player ignites a new vertex in a chosen colour. The optimal achievable count, called the plurality number, is expressed through Hamming distances to a binary code associated with the graph. The authors determine exact plurality numbers for certain signed paths and prove hardness results for computing or approximating it.

entry.title: Optimizing simulation and data pipelines for experiments on exascale computers
entry.summary: Real-time Optimization of Simulation and Data Processing Pipelines for Experiments on Exascale Computing Platforms arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper addresses how large experiments in high-energy physics and cosmology, which generate growing volumes of data, can use exascale computing resources efficiently. The authors propose a multi-stage task scheduling approach and demonstrate it on a Monte Carlo simulation pipeline from the Short-Baseline Near Detector (SBND). They also present theoretical and numerical tools for modeling task scheduling, which can help identify optimal strategies and choose resources for a given problem size.

entry.title: Conditional Correctness in List Decoding: When a Later Second Codeword Boosts Confidence in the First
entry.summary: Conditional Correctness in List Decoding: How a Late Second Codeword Can Rescue Confidence in the First arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper studies how the likelihood ranks of noise sequences in list decoding relate to the posterior probability that a decoding is correct. Under a random codebook model, the authors show that soft-output expressions for list decoding exactly match finite-blocklength conditional correctness probabilities, and they characterize the asymptotic reliability of the first list entry under hard-decision maximum likelihood decoding. The reliability depends only on the first, second, and last ranks. For list size two, a sufficiently late second entry can make the first entry asymptotically correct even when its rank alone suggests otherwise.

entry.title: Topology-aware integrated sensing, communication, and charging for large-scale low-altitude wireless networks
entry.summary: Topology-Aware Integrated Sensing, Communication, Charging in Massive Low-Altitude Wireless Network arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper addresses low-altitude wireless networks that must support sensing, communication, and charging at once, which creates tightly coupled optimization problems. The authors propose a unified topology-aware framework that represents terrestrial and airborne devices as nodes and their interactions as edges in a bipartite graph. Based on this representation, they develop a low-complexity topology reconfiguration algorithm using a unified resource-adjustment rule. Simulations show better multi-functional coordination efficiency than state-of-the-art methods, with robustness and scalability in scenarios with many ground and airborne users.

entry.title: From Alert Floods to Precedence Forests: LOGOS, a Zero-Prior-Knowledge Incident Triage System
entry.summary: From Alert Floods to Precedence Forests: Zero-Prior-Knowledge Incident Triage with LOGOS arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper asks whether failure propagation can be isolated using only raw, unannotated text logs. The authors present LOGOS, an unsupervised system that uses entity-event co-occurrence and temporal precedence to compress millions of log lines into a compact precedence forest. Tested on 25 production enterprise outages and 12 open-source issues without any prior knowledge, it reports a median runtime of 4.5 minutes, a median 99.8% noise reduction, and a mean recall of 0.76.

entry.title: Feature freshness budgets for real-time ML inference under stream lag
entry.summary: Feature Freshness Budgets for Real-Time ML Inference Under Stream Lag arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 The paper models an online feature store as a materialized view over an event stream and defines a per-feature freshness budget, the gap between a feature's decision window and the staleness imposed by serving. It proves a per-feature staleness bound and a closed-form threshold below which a feature cannot be served within budget. The results are validated in a discrete-event simulation and on a real Kafka, Redis, and PostgreSQL pipeline, where the predicted threshold reproduces. The authors find the main simulation-to-infrastructure gap stems from sampling-phase artifacts rather than latency, and randomizing the phase reduces the drop-rate error to 0.018. ★★★★ Notable: Formalizes feature freshness as a bounded budget with a closed-form threshold, validated on real Kafka, Redis, PostgreSQL pipelines, and identifies a phase-locking simulation bias.

entry.title: MoE-CORE: A system that coordinates expert offloading and storage to run large Mixture-of-Experts models on limited device memory.
entry.summary: MoE-CORE: Coordinated Expert Offloading and Residency for Memory-Constrained MoE Inference arXiv · Oct 2, 2026 This paper presents MoE-CORE, a system for running Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model inference when device memory is limited. It loads complete expert layers in alternating buffers during prefill and, during decoding, uses layer-wise cache sizing, routing-history-aware replacement, and cross-layer prefetching to reduce host-to-device transfers. The authors report substantially lower mean time per output token than the evaluated vLLM Prefetch configuration on DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A8 and GLM-5.2-W4A8C8.

entry.title: ePACT: An energy-performance-aware controller that tracks hourly power commitments for LLM serving
entry.summary: ePACT: Energy-Performance-Aware Commitment Tracking for LLM Serving arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 The paper argues that cutting LLM serving energy alone does not guarantee lower costs, because deviations from preset electricity commitments can be costly, especially when overuse and underuse are priced asymmetrically. The authors propose ePACT, a two-level controller that adjusts serving capacity and GPU clocks while meeting request-level service requirements. In full-day trace simulations on H20 and H200 GPU pools, ePACT reduces the asymmetric deviation cost by 73.8% and 75.7% relative to vLLM while retaining near-vLLM SLO attainment.

entry.title: Storage codes from binary BCH codes that approach unit rate
entry.summary: Asymptotically unit-rate storage codes from binary BCH codes arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 A storage code assigns symbols to graph vertices so each symbol can be recovered from its neighbors. The paper proves that binary full-parity storage codes on triangle-free coset graphs of primitive BCH codes have rate approaching one for any fixed error-correction capability of at least two. For the double-error-correcting family over F_{2^m}, the storage deficiency is shown to be Θ(((1+√5)/4)^m).

entry.title: Token-based economy for fairer, efficient highway congestion control using express lanes
entry.summary: Token Economy Design for Fair and Efficient Highway Congestion Management with Express Lanes arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper studies a non-monetary token economy for allocating highway lanes, aiming to improve fairness without reducing traffic efficiency. High-occupancy vehicles get unrestricted express lane access, while other users earn and spend tokens to switch between regular and express lanes. In a microscopic traffic simulation using real-world demand data, the proposed prices produced nearly the same average travel time as a scenario with no reserved express lane, while substantially reducing urgency-weighted perceived travel time.

entry.title: Giving LLMs social value profiles makes their play in a social dilemma more human-like
entry.summary: Conditioning LLMs on Social Value Orientation improves behavioural alignment in a sequential social dilemma arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 The authors test eight large language models on two versions of the Centipede Game and compare their default choices with human experimental data. The models' default strategies vary widely and are generally far from the human reference. When conditioned on Social Value Orientation (SVO) profiles drawn from human participants, alignment with human behaviour improves by up to 70%, and higher SVO values reduce the probability of stopping the game.

entry.title: Speeding up MPI programs by letting compute-heavy and memory-heavy parts drift out of step
entry.summary: Exploiting the Interplay of Compute- and Memory-Bound kernels in MPI Applications arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 The paper shows that in MPI applications with little communication that alternate between compute-bound and memory-bound phases, communication stalls can unintentionally ease memory-bandwidth contention. The authors demonstrate this with a parallel optical flow solver combining ray tracing and an optical flow kernel, achieving considerable speedup through desynchronization. A tunable microbenchmark and a bandwidth-aware simulator are used to study and validate the effect.

entry.title: Optimal Universal Coding of Integers: Numerically Determining the Minimum Expansion Factor
entry.summary: Optimal Universal Coding of Integers arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper studies universal coding of integers (UCI), which assigns binary codewords to positive integers so that the average codeword length stays within K times max{1,H(P)} for every nonincreasing source distribution. The authors show that the worst-case ratio for any universal code is attained by a family of one-point-plus-uniform-tail distributions. They also introduce a UCI inequality, analogous to the Kraft inequality for prefix codes, which yields an equivalent definition of the optimal minimum expansion factor C*. Numerical computation gives C* = 2.000124757036101…, with the first fifteen decimal digits certified.

entry.title: Agentic Wireless Digital Twin Building and Calibration from Real Measurements
entry.summary: Agentic Wireless Digital Twin Construction and Calibration Using Real-World Measurements arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper proposes AWDT, an agent-based framework that automatically builds and calibrates wireless digital twins. Three agents handle the propagation environment, base station and sector configuration, and radio material properties, refining the model using differences between smartphone-measured RSRP and ray-tracing predictions. In real-world experiments, the RSRP prediction MAE dropped from 11.46 dB to 5.25 dB. Evaluation with an independent measurement system also showed transfer across devices with lightweight device-specific bias adaptation.

entry.title: GPU-Initiated Communication: A Low-Level Performance Dissection
entry.summary: GPU-Initiated Communication: Dissecting Down to the Bone arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper examines how GPU threads post RDMA operations directly to the network interface card, a mechanism used by NVSHMEM, NCCL GIN, and DeepEP. The authors build minimal GPU and CPU-proxy transports and benchmark them against several libraries on NVIDIA H100, H200, B200, and GB200 systems. They report that a minimal GPU path issues an operation in 0.7 µs and completes it in 4.0 µs, with library overheads adding up to 4.6 µs. The paper concludes that the submission path alone does not predict overall communication performance. ★★★★ Notable: Decomposes GPU-to-NIC communication via minimal transports and measures multiple libraries on several platforms, separating hardware from library costs.

entry.title: Joint communication and sensing coverage for UAV corridors with beam misalignment
entry.summary: Communication and Sensing Coverage of UAV Corridor under Beam Misalignment Error arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper studies joint communication and sensing (JCAS) coverage probability for a terrestrial base station using a realistic 3D 3GPP antenna pattern, with UAV users deployed in a finite cylindrical aerial corridor. The base station uses radar sensing to track a known UAV, under a 3D beam misalignment error modeled as multivariate normal. Exact analytical expressions for JCAS coverage probability are derived under clutter and uplink interference. The results show corridor-length saturation at high UAV heights and a beamwidth trade-off between interference suppression and misalignment sensitivity.

entry.title: Joint Communication and Sensing in Aerial Corridors: A Stochastic Geometry Model
entry.summary: Joint Communication and Sensing in Aerial Corridors: A Novel Stochastic Geometry Framework arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper studies how well a drone base station can both communicate and sense in an aerial corridor filled with drone users. The corridor is modeled as a finite cylinder, with users randomly placed in three dimensions and the base station tracking a known user with radar. The authors derive exact formulas for coverage probability under clutter and uplink interference. They find that more directional base station antenna beams improve performance noticeably, especially in shorter corridors.

entry.title: UAV attitude-aware trajectory and attitude co-design for covert communication
entry.summary: Exploiting UAV Attitude for Covert Communications: Dynamics-Consistent Trajectory-Attitude Co-Design arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 Existing UAV covert communication trajectory designs usually treat the drone as a point mass and ignore how maneuvers affect antenna orientation. This paper studies a rotary-wing UAV with a directional antenna sending confidential data to a legitimate receiver while a warden is present, explicitly modeling acceleration-induced attitude and its effect on channel gain. It derives a covertness constraint using KL divergence at the warden and jointly optimizes trajectory and attitude with an MM-based algorithm to maximize average covert rate. The framework is also extended to a robust design under imperfect attitude control.</en

entry.title: RapidMoE: Adaptive Residual Offloading for Faster Large-Scale MoE Inference
entry.summary: RapidMoE: Exploiting Cross-Asymmetry via Adaptive Residual Offloading for Large-Scale MoE Inference arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper addresses the mismatch between large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models and heterogeneous CPU-GPU hardware, where PCIe bandwidth limits and heavy CPU computation reduce efficiency. It proposes RapidMoE, a residual offloading system that shifts offloading from the expert level to the bit level, using compact data representation, dual-path routing matched to hardware, and balanced scheduling. The authors also introduce a runtime arbitration method to adjust critical experts. Experiments report up to 3.5x decoding speedup and 2.1x prefill speedup over state-of-the-art offloading systems.

entry.title: Serving Revisable Agent Tasks Through Versioned Execution
entry.summary: Serving a Revisable World: Versioned Execution for Interruptible Agents arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 The paper presents RETIRE, a serving control-plane design for LLM agents whose running tasks get revised. Each execution version holds the authority to publish output or install state, so obsolete work is revoked first and the completed prefix that a successor can inherit is certified. The design is implemented in vLLM. In controlled paired experiments, it reduces the median revision-to-successor time-to-first-token by 17.1%. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes versioned execution unifying obsolete-work revocation and KV state inheritance, implemented in vLLM with paired experiments showing a 17.1% median TTFT reduction.

entry.title: Fair, non-wasteful matching of families and daycare places, including siblings and already-enrolled children
entry.summary: Fairness and Non-wastefulness in Matching with Siblings and Initial Enrollments: Compatibility and Complexity arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper studies matching between families and daycare centers, where a family may have several children with joint preferences and some children are already enrolled and seeking transfers. The authors introduce resettlement, which lets displaced families return to their initial assignments, and give a greedy algorithm showing that matchings satisfying non-wastefulness and resettlement-based fairness exist. They also analyze computational complexity, finding that some existence questions are NP-complete and computing resettlement-based outcomes is PLS-hard.

entry.title: Seamless reconfiguration for DAG-based Byzantine atomic broadcast in asynchronous networks
entry.summary: Seamless Reconfiguration for DAG-BFT arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper proposes a seamless reconfiguration protocol for asynchronous DAG-based Byzantine atomic broadcast, which adds or removes nodes. Existing DAG-based BFT protocols assume a static set of processes, and prior reconfiguration approaches either pause the system or wait for a predetermined epoch boundary. The proposed protocol lets the DAG keep growing while membership and quorum thresholds change, without halting the system. The authors state it is the first such protocol for fully asynchronous networks.

entry.title: Reading While Writing: Baseline Data Needs for Molecular Neural Interfaces
entry.summary: Reading While Writing: Baseline Information Requirements for Molecular Neural Interfaces arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper studies molecular neural interfaces that both deliver and sense a neurotransmitter, and how they can estimate endogenous release despite their own chemical input. The authors analyze two exchanging regions with shared saturable uptake and show that an unknown resting concentration difference leaves the source region's uptake uncertain. A dopamine-inspired example and a Gaussian observation model are used to show how delivery and baseline information affect release classification.

entry.title: MANTA: ML-Augmented Tiering Advisor for Smarter Memory Page Placement
entry.summary: MANTA: Machine Learning Augmented Tiering Advisor arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 Memory tiering combines fast DRAM with slower tiers such as CXL-attached memory to expand capacity. The paper introduces ChOMP, an offline optimizer used as a reference, and a trace-driven simulator that reveals opportunities for online policies. It then presents MANTA, which predicts page usefulness from runtime access features using a lightweight learned model integrated into ARMS. On eight emulated CXL workloads at 4 GB fast memory, MANTA achieves geometric-mean speedups over ARMS of 1.12× on Linux 6.2 and 1.08× on Linux 6.18, and 1.69× across six Optane workloads.

entry.title: Ditto: Generalized Reconfigurable Linearizable Reads
entry.summary: Ditto: Generalized Reconfigurable Linearizable Reads arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper studies how to make linearizable reads faster in distributed datastores without giving up consistency. It classifies existing read algorithms into a generalized space and analyzes their latencies mathematically, revealing two fundamental tradeoffs. The authors propose a new algorithm, Pairwise Quorums, and Ditto, a system that reconfigures across this space at runtime as network and workload conditions change. They claim that together these subsume existing algorithms, being either strictly better or matching them where a real tradeoff exists.

entry.title: MegaFlux: Skew-resilient MoE megakernels with pipelined expert replication
entry.summary: MegaFlux: Skew-Resilient MoE Megakernels via Pipelined Expert Replication arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper addresses slowdowns in mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, where uneven routing overloads some GPUs while others sit idle. It presents MegaFlux, which decides at runtime whether to replicate popular experts and pipelines the resulting weight transfers and backward gradient reductions with expert computation. Across 147 configurations per direction on eight NVIDIA B200 GPUs, it reports geometric-mean speedups of 1.45x for forward and 1.28x for backward over fixed expert placement.

entry.title: Forming Alliances Under Uncertainty: A General Lotto Study
entry.summary: Forming Alliances in the Fog of War: A General Lotto Perspective arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper studies whether two players fighting a shared opponent can benefit from alliances when they only partly know each other's or the adversary's resource budgets. It uses the coalitional General Lotto game, where players allocate budgets across valued contests. The authors characterize which games admit a budget transfer that helps both players under multiplicative uncertainty. They show such robust transfers exist in a positive-measure set of games at every uncertainty level.

entry.title: Shaping and modulation augmentation for LDPC-coded QPSK
entry.summary: Modulation Augmentation and Constellation Shaping for LDPC-Coded QPSK arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper adds a short shaping code to LDPC-coded QPSK so that some codeword bits control how often lower- and higher-energy constellation points are sent. The lower-energy points are chosen more often, producing a Gaussian-like symbol distribution. The receiver refines shaping-bit likelihoods using LDPC decoder feedback, and the shaping codebook, bit mapping and constellations are jointly optimized. The authors report gains of up to 0.6 dB over 5G NR LDPC-coded QPSK and 0.53 dB over QAM-16.

entry.title: Market design for two-sided ad auctions with autobidders: which mechanisms still work when both buyers and sellers are strategic
entry.summary: Two-sided Market Design Meets Autobidding arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 The paper studies two-sided markets in which autobidders, such as Return-on-Spend (RoS) value maximizers, participate on one or both sides. It shows that, without prior information, many incentive-compatible, budget-balanced mechanisms have unbounded Price of Anarchy for liquid gains from trade when value maximizers are present. It also finds that McAfee's Trade Reduction mechanism keeps a constant Price of Anarchy for liquid welfare under RoS bidding. With distributional information, the authors design a mechanism that achieves first-best liquid welfare when at least one side consists of RoS maximizers, contrasting with the Myerson-Satterthwaite impossibility. ★★★★ Notable: First study of two-sided autobidder markets, with negative and positive results, and a first-best mechanism under distributional information contrasting Myerson-Satterthwaite impossibility.

entry.title: L2R-EV: Learning Which Repairs to Make in Electric Ride-Pooling with Limited Charger Queues
entry.summary: L2R-EV: Learning What to Repair in Electric Ride-Pooling with Finite Charger Queues arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 The paper studies electric ride-pooling, where passenger service, routes, batteries, and limited chargers must be managed together. The authors build a discrete-event simulator and add a learned repair layer that reassigns uncollected passengers, guided by a supervised score and a two-stage PPO policy. On 12 held-out Manhattan episodes, supervised repair cut operational cost by 6.57% versus no repair and won in all 12 episodes, while queue-aware charging reduced waiting by 41.0%.

entry.title: LatencyLab: a DPDK-based tool for measuring P4 pipeline latency on FPGA SmartNICs
entry.summary: LatencyLab: A DPDK-Based P4 Pipeline Latency Measurement Framework for FPGA SmartNICs arXiv · Oct 1, 2026 This paper presents LatencyLab, a DPDK-based framework that measures how much latency a P4 program adds on an FPGA SmartNIC, without needing PTP support or clock synchronization.
