A switch duplicates each probe packet to two ports, one through the VitisNetP4 pipeline and one through a matched bypass path, and the arrival-time difference isolates pipeline latency. The authors evaluated four VitisNetP4 programs on an AMD Alveo U280 and report tight, reproducible latency distributions, with two independent checks agreeing with the measurements.[18]

entry.title: Generalized Prophet Inequalities for Online Auctions: Agents with Budgets and Mixed Objectives
entry.summary: Generalized Prophet Inequalities for Online Auctions arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper studies prophet inequalities for online auctions, a setting that classically assumes agents maximize quasi-linear utility. The authors model agents' budgets and varying objectives, such as value maximization in autobidding, as stochastic inputs alongside valuations. They analyze anonymous posted-price mechanisms and generalize the balanced prices framework to incorporate budgets and mixed objectives. The paper shows constant competitive ratios in several central settings, including agents with subadditive valuations, and identifies trade-offs between competitive ratio and price sensitivity. It also gives a general reduction from budgeted settings to budget-free value maximizers. ★★★★ Notable: Extends prophet inequalities to budgeted, mixed-objective agents, proving constant competitive ratios and a reduction to budget-free value maximizers.

entry.title: Darpan: A Digital Twin Framework for Next-Generation Computing Continuum Decisions
entry.summary: Darpan: A Digital Twin Framework for the Next-Generation Computing Continuum arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper proposes Darpan, a digital twin framework for applications spanning devices, edge, fog, and cloud. A physical side runs real applications and observes their state, while a digital side keeps an executable virtual copy updated to evaluate candidate decisions from the same starting point. The selected decision is validated against the latest physical state before execution. The authors report a mean absolute error of 0.485 s for predicted response time and 93.1% scale-out efficiency at 40 nodes on real DAG workloads.

entry.title: Adaptive power allocation to improve mission efficiency for coordinated low-altitude aircraft swarms
entry.summary: Mission Efficiency Optimization in Low-Altitude Economy: Adaptive Power Allocation for Coordinating Heterogeneous Aircraft Swarms arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper studies how multiple heterogeneous low-altitude aircraft cooperate on complex missions, with some handling sensing, communication, computing, and execution. The authors introduce operational-capability entropy to quantify each aircraft's effective work capability. They formulate a power allocation problem that minimizes a linear quadratic regulator cost as a mission-efficiency metric, considering channel conditions. The problem is split into two convex subproblems solved iteratively with closed-form solutions, and simulations show the scheme outperforms traditional approaches.

entry.title: Comparing adaptive Byzantine quorum systems to reduce latency in wide-area networks
entry.summary: Exploring Adaptive Byzantine Quorum Systems to Improve Latency in the WAN arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 In Byzantine fault-tolerant replication, a quorum of replicas must vote on a value before it is decided, and the quorum's size and makeup affect client latency over wide-area networks. Existing quorum designs are usually tied to different protocol implementations, which makes fair comparison difficult. The authors extend BFT-SMaRt with a modular quorum-system abstraction so that several quorum constructions can run in the same framework with the same optimizations. They then use network simulation to study how these constructions affect client-observed latency.

entry.title: Age of information distributions in an Erlang loss system with shared servers
entry.summary: Distribution of Age of Information in the Erlang Loss System arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper derives exact distributions of age of information (AoI) and peak AoI (PAoI) in a bufferless M/M/c/c Erlang loss system, where Poisson-arriving updates from one or more sources share c servers. Three policies handle arrivals when all servers are busy: blocking, preempting a random same-source update, or preempting the stalest one. Using an absorbing Markov chain method, the authors obtain matrix-exponential distributions, which extend to multiple sources affected only by aggregate update rates.

entry.title: Kirin: An orchestrator for cloud-native WebAssembly services
entry.summary: Kirin: Cloud-native WebAssembly Service Orchestration arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper presents Kirin, an orchestrator for cloud-native WebAssembly services that handles resource scheduling, lifecycle management, scaling, and request routing. The authors evaluate Kirin against container-based deployments across several service workloads. Results are promising for service lifecycle management, while known limitations remain for CPU-intensive workloads. For typical service workloads, Kirin performs competitively, suggesting WebAssembly could be a viable cloud-native deployment option.

entry.title: Tight liquid welfare bounds for budget-constrained auctions via LP duality
entry.summary: Tight Liquid Welfare Guarantees for Auctions with Budgets via LP Duality arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper studies the efficiency of auctions with budget-constrained bidders and derives tight price of anarchy bounds for coarse correlated equilibria. It introduces a general framework that reduces these guarantees to finding feasible solutions to the dual of a linear program, along with a new smoothness notion for budget-constrained settings. Using this framework, the authors obtain tight liquid welfare guarantees for many auction formats and new lower bounds for the budget-free uniform price and generalized second-price auctions. ★★★★★ Notable: Proposes an LP-duality framework and new smoothness notion, yielding tight PoA bounds across many auctions and matching a known upper bound.

entry.title: Version Age-of-Information-Based Semantic Secrecy Region Analysis: examines semantic secrecy in wireless status updates, balancing information freshness against eavesdropping.
entry.summary: Version Age-of-Information-based Semantic Secrecy Region Analysis arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper studies semantic secrecy in wireless status-update systems using Version Age of Information (VAoI). It models the tradeoff between informative updates and confidentiality with a three-node wiretap channel. The authors introduce the semantic secrecy region (SSR), analyze it geometrically, and derive closed-form expressions for the destination's average VAoI and the eavesdropper's semantic asymmetry probability using a two-dimensional Markov chain. For Rayleigh fading channels, they characterize the optimal SSR boundary and power allocation, and numerical results show that optimized power allocation enlarges the secrecy region compared with fixed-power benchmarks.

entry.title: Federated Calibration of UAV Motion Uncertainty in Multi-Operator ISAC
entry.summary: Federated Calibration of Motion Uncertainty for UAV Tracking in Multi-Operator ISAC Systems arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper studies UAV tracking in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems with multiple operators, where raw sensing data, channel information, and transmit decisions stay local. The authors propose a two-timescale framework: slow-timescale calibration of motion uncertainty using local radar innovations, and online fusion of track estimates via covariance intersection with predictive beamforming. Simulations show improved tracking-uncertainty consistency under motion model mismatch, and about 31% lower RMSE than communication-only transmission design with less than 2% extra power.

entry.title: Fair Outcome Prospects Encourage Prosocial Behaviour in the Centipede Game
entry.summary: The prospect of a fair outcome triggers prosocial behaviour in the Centipede Game arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This behavioural experiment studies how people make sequential resource-exchange decisions in the Incremental Centipede Game, comparing a zero-payoff deadline treatment with a treatment ending in a fair split. Even though the fair outcome is uncertain, it moves participants beyond self-interest. An evolutionary model indicates that the fair split shifts play toward mutually beneficial strategies when players are sufficiently prosocial and use probabilistic strategies.

entry.title: FissionReady: Joint Workload and Power Scheduling for Small Modular Reactor Data Centers
entry.summary: FissionReady: Joint Workload and Power Scheduling for Data Centers Powered by Small Modular Reactors arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper presents FissionReady, a scheduler for data centers powered by small modular reactors (SMRs). It tracks each module's fuel age, xenon state, and remaining flexibility to set per-module operating limits, then coordinates load-following, batch deferral, and grid purchases through a two-timescale optimization. Compared with a same-sized base configuration, the authors report zero involuntary shutdowns and zero batch deadline misses, with water use reduced by about one-third and grid cost by about half.

entry.title: Communication-efficient (1+ε)Δ edge coloring and the Lovász local lemma
entry.summary: Communication-Efficient (1+ǎrepsilon)Δ-Edge Coloring and Lovász Local Lemma arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper studies edge coloring in the two-party edge-partition model, where Alice and Bob each hold part of the edges and must jointly produce a proper coloring with little communication. The authors give a public-coin Las Vegas protocol that finds a (1+ε)Δ edge coloring for sufficiently large Δ, using expected O(ne^{-γΔ}+1) bits and O(log n/Δ+1) rounds. They also develop a two-party constructive Lovász local lemma, which they apply to several other classical problems. ★★★★ Notable: Introduces a new randomized coloring procedure and a two-party constructive LLL, reducing colors to (1+ε)Δ and communication substantially; solid analysis, relevant to a subfield.

entry.title: Multi-View LP Bounds for Locally Recoverable Codes with Availability
entry.summary: Multi-View Block Distance Distributions and Linear Programming Bounds for Locally Recoverable Codes with Availability arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 The paper develops a multi-view linear-programming framework for locally recoverable codes with fixed availability a, recording Hamming distances across partitioned helper-set blocks. Constraints from counting identities, product-Krawtchouk positivity, and collision inequalities give a polynomial-size relaxation for arbitrary finite-field codes. For availability 2, exact rational certificates establish M_max values of 8, 27 and 64 for three parameter sets. The four-block bound is strictly stronger than both coarser models.

entry.title: Vosti: A Verified Engine for Bitwise-Deterministic LLM Inference
entry.summary: Vosti: Specifying, Implementing, and Verifying Deterministic LLM Inference arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 The paper formally defines deterministic LLM inference as producing bitwise-identical logits for the same prompt and initial sampler state under a fixed model and deployment configuration. The authors find that production modes such as vLLM's batch-invariant mode and SGLang's deterministic mode yield different logits under some execution variations. They present Vosti, an inference engine built against this specification, with a Verus inductive proof for scheduling and the prefix-sharing KV cache and a Triton analyzer proving kernel output equality. Vosti reports identical logits across all tested variations and performance comparable to vLLM's batch-invariant mode on decode-heavy workloads. ★★★★ Notable: Formalizes deterministic LLM inference and verifies scheduling, KV-cache, and kernels with Verus and a Triton analyzer, beyond empirical batch-invariance guarantees.

entry.title: Exact embeddings of complete bipartite graphs and non-embeddable lattices under information distance
entry.summary: Complete bipartite embeddings, lattice non-embeddability, and non-Euclidean powers of information distance arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 The paper encodes vertices of finite complete bipartite graphs as binary strings at each scale, so that information distances approximate scaled graph distances with a constant additive error. This resolves an open problem of Hutter on scale-embeddings of such graphs and shows that no positive power of information distance is exactly representable in a real Hilbert space. The authors also prove that integer lattices admit no scale-embedding and extend this conclusion to (R^m, ||·||_1).

entry.title: Efficient HPC Systems for AI Agents: Challenges and Opportunities
entry.summary: Towards Efficient HPC Systems for Agents: Challenges and Opportunities arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper examines how coding agents have become real users of high-performance computing systems, while HPC abstractions, interfaces, and policies were designed for human-driven workflows. The authors report that agent users are 19.5% of observed users but account for 55.8% of job submissions, 29.1% of CPU core-hours, and 42.7% of GPU-hours. They argue that facilities should co-design systems that treat agents as first-class principals, and outline challenges and opportunities in compute, storage, agent memory, and safety.

entry.title: Keeping Provenance in Shared KV Caches to Prevent Unsafe Reuse in LLM Serving
entry.summary: Preserving Provenance in Shared KV Caches for LLM Serving arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 The paper finds that LLM serving systems keep provenance such as adapter and weight configuration in local prefix caches, but the shared KV-cache tier keys entries only by token content and coarse model metadata. This lets identical tokens from incompatible contexts collide; cross-adapter collisions cut accuracy from 0.94 to 0.64 in the authors' experiments on vLLM and SGLang. The authors propose a KV provenance contract that binds provenance into lookup and store keys through a canonical descriptor, implemented across three cache paths. The implementation eliminates unsafe reuse while keeping legitimate sharing, with hit-path latency changes within 0.34 ms. ★★★★ Notable: First systematic study of provenance loss in shared KV caches, with broad runtime experiments across engines and models; practically impactful for LLM serving.

entry.title: Efficiency of Generalized Proportional First-Price Auctions Under Auto-bidding
entry.summary: Efficiency of Generalized Proportional First-Price Auctions Under Auto-bidding arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper studies how efficiently auctions allocate ad slots when advertisers use auto-bidding with return-on-spend constraints. It measures efficiency loss via the Price of Anarchy across prior-free auction formats. For two bidders, the standard proportional first-price auction achieves a tight PoA of at most 1.5. For n bidders, setting the exponent to 2n yields a PoA of 2 minus 1/(4n+1), beating the deterministic barrier of 2. ★★★★ Notable: Proves tight PoA of 1.5 for two bidders with matching lower bound, and breaks the barrier of 2 for all finite n.

entry.title: Efficient client selection for federated learning as a service in multi-application IoT systems
entry.summary: Enabling Efficient Client Selection in FL-as-a-Service for Multi-Application based Society 5.0 arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper examines federated learning as a service (FLaaS) in IoT, where models are trained across devices without sharing raw data, enabling collaboration across applications. The authors propose selecting client nodes for model training based on delay, energy consumption, and link status. They evaluate the method on a Human Activity Recognition dataset under simulated IoT network conditions, comparing it with random and Q-learning based selection. The reported results show improved delay and energy efficiency while maintaining communication performance.

entry.title: Auctions with Price Predictions: Designing Single-Item Auctions Using a Predicted Revenue-Maximizing Price
entry.summary: Auctions with Price Predictions arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 The paper designs auctions for selling one item in unlimited supply, given only a single prediction of the revenue-maximizing uniform price rather than predictions of each bidder's value. The authors characterize the Pareto frontier of consistency and robustness achievable by any universally truthful auction. They show that randomizing between posting the predicted price and running an optimal prior-free fallback auction is Pareto-optimal. The paper also extends the results to graceful revenue degradation with prediction accuracy and studies learning such predictions from historical market data. ★★★★ Notable: Designs auctions from one predicted revenue-maximizing price, characterizes the consistency-robustness Pareto frontier, and gives a learning-theoretic path from historical data.

entry.title: Rotatable antennas for space-air-ground networks: opportunities and challenges
entry.summary: Rotatable Antenna-Enabled Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks: Opportunities and Challenges arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This article examines how rotatable antenna (RA) technology, which adjusts beam direction mechanically or electronically while keeping antenna positions fixed, can support communication and sensing in space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs). It explains RA's role in wide-area coverage, dynamic directional transmission, and cooperative sensing, and discusses design challenges such as channel acquisition and cross-segment coordination. An RA array prototype and two simulation studies are presented to illustrate feasibility and potential performance gains.

entry.title: Why does scale-invariant regret matching converge linearly at the last iterate?
entry.summary: Why Last-Iterate Scale-Invariant Regret Matching Converges Linearly? arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 The paper studies IREG-PRM+, which normalizes cumulative regret by its own norm and reaches optimal regret without knowing the payoff scale. On zero-sum matrix games it converges linearly in the last iterate, and the authors attribute this to norm saturation, where the regret norm rises to a finite limit and freezes the step size. They prove this always happens and that the last-iterate Nash gap vanishes on every matrix game. Near a unique strictly complementary equilibrium they give a closed-form linear rate and an observable ratio certificate. ★★★★ Notable: Explains linear last-iterate convergence of scale-invariant regret matching via norm saturation, with explicit bounds and closed-form rates, backed by a sizable testbed.

entry.title: An information identity showing the geometry behind rare deviation events
entry.summary: An information identity reveals the geometry of deviation events arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 The paper studies the probability of a deviation event, where the empirical measure of n independent draws falls in a set of distributions. At every n, the exponent of this probability splits into two nonnegative terms: a rate, equal to n times the relative entropy of a typical draw's distribution under the event relative to the population, and a dependence term among the draws, measured by total correlation. The relative sizes of the two terms depend on the geometry of the set, which the paper examines.

entry.title: A transmitter design that adapts to the receiver for a 200 Gbps C-band optical access network.
entry.summary: Receiver-Informed Transmitter for 200Gbps C-Band Direct-Detection PON With FFE-Free ONU arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper proposes and numerically demonstrates a receiver-informed transmitter (RITX) waveform design for 200 Gb/s PAM-4 C-band direct-detection passive optical networks. Using 50 GHz optoelectronics, RITX reaches N1/E1 loss classes with an FFE-free ONU and supports a 40 km reach. At 1:64 and 1:128 splits, it yields network-wide complexity savings of 48.1% and 66.7%, respectively.

entry.title: Simple Mechanisms in Matching Markets: A Tight e-Approximation for Gains from Trade
entry.summary: The Power of Simple Mechanisms: A Tight e-Approximation for Gains from Trade in Matching Markets arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper studies how well simple mechanisms approximate gains from trade (GFT) in two-sided matching markets with independent buyer values and seller costs. It shows that the Generalized Random-Offerer mechanism achieves an exact worst-case approximation ratio of e relative to first-best GFT, improving the previous 3.15 bound. The authors also construct markets with regular distributions and a single knapsack constraint showing this guarantee is tight. ★★★★★ Notable: Establishes GRO's exact worst-case ratio e with matching tightness, substantially improving the prior 3.15 bound and resolving the question for this mechanism.

entry.title: How GPU server layout, parallelism and congestion control jointly affect MoE inference speed
entry.summary: Joint Effects of GPU Server Topology, Parallelism, and Congestion Control on MoE Inference: A Controlled Simulation Study arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper uses ASTRA-sim with an NS-3 backend to simulate MoE model inference across 32 GPU ranks under controlled settings. It tests six server topologies, four TP/EP partitions, two TP collective algorithms and four network congestion-control modes, giving 768 deterministic simulations. The authors find that exposed communication accounts for 89.9% to 95.8% of mean completion time, and that topology, parallelism, collective implementation and congestion control jointly determine completion time.

entry.title: Innovation-Based Sampling: Conveying Information Through the Direction and Timing of New Information
entry.summary: Innovation-Based Sampling for New Information arXiv · Sep 30, 2026 This paper introduces innovation-based sampling of continuous stochastic processes, generating a sample only when the process reveals sufficiently new information relative to earlier samples. For a Wiener process, it characterizes the direction, timing, and frequency of innovations, showing they become sparser over time so the sampling rate vanishes asymptotically. The paper also studies remote estimation from sparse innovations, finding that the absence of an innovation carries information and yields substantially lower mean-square error than a conventional zero-order hold estimator.

entry.title: Emulating FP64 matrix products with low-precision INT8, FP8 and FP4 operations
entry.summary: FP64 Is All You Want, INT8 Is All You Need, FP4/6/8 Is All You Have arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper treats Ozaki scheme II and its FP8 and FP4 variants as one family that emulates FP64 matrix products using residues modulo coprime moduli. It frames choosing a scheme as a combinatorial problem that minimizes the number of low-precision GEMMs and derives lower bounds on that count. Implemented on three Blackwell GPUs, the INT8, FP8 and FP4 schemes run faster than native FP64, up to 83x on B300. ★★★★★ Notable: Unifies Ozaki-style schemes as a combinatorial optimization with GEMM lower bounds, yielding first FP6 schemes and measured speedups up to 83x on Blackwell GPUs.

entry.title: Optimal codes that correct up to t deletions in permutations
entry.summary: Order-Optimal Systematic Permutation Codes for Correcting t Deletions arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper constructs systematic permutation codes that correct multiple deletions under two models: symbol-invariant deletions (SIDs) and permutation-invariant deletions (PIDs). For any fixed t≥1 and large n, the encoders insert redundancy symbols while preserving the order of the message symbols. The redundancy is (7t−1)log n+O_t(1) bits for PIDs and 4t log n+O_t(1) bits for SIDs. Encoding and decoding run in n^{O(t)} time.

entry.title: MEDEM: A Design Method for Multi-Engine Deep Learning Accelerators
entry.summary: MEDEM: Multi-Engine DL Accelerator Design Methodology arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper proposes MEDEM, a systematic methodology for designing deep learning accelerators that combine multiple complementary engines. It co-designs candidate engines and selects the combination that minimizes aggregate execution cost under a resource budget. The authors report geometric-mean improvements of up to 4.84x in energy-delay product and 1.59x in throughput over state-of-the-art designs.

entry.title: Sharp lower bound on second-best welfare in bilateral and matching markets when values are private
entry.summary: Sharp Second-Best Welfare in Bilateral and Matching Markets arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper determines the exact ratio of second-best to first-best social welfare when buyers' and sellers' values are private. The ratio is approximately 0.8882516903 for arbitrary priors and 0.9113893681 when buyers have monotone hazard rates. Both constants are already attained in bilateral trade and extend to matching markets. The authors give variational characterizations of the constants and reproducible interval certificates for numerical evaluation. ★★★★ Notable: Gives sharp second-best to first-best welfare ratios for bilateral and matching markets, proven tight for arbitrary priors and MHR buyers.

entry.title: Matroid packing games: how to fairly split shared value (core and nucleolus)
entry.summary: Matroid Packing Games: The Core and the Nucleolus arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies the matroid base packing problem using cooperative game theory and defines a matroid base packing game. It extends the network strength game of Baiou and Barahona (2020) from graphic matroids to general matroids. Using the exchange structure of matroids, the authors build a graph-theoretic framework for analyzing the game's core and nucleolus. The framework gives a compact condition for core nonemptiness and polynomial-time algorithms for testing it, finding a core allocation, and computing the nucleolus.

entry.title: Delay guarantees for SIC-decoded VLSF codes under hardcore spatial regulation
entry.summary: Performance Guarantees of SIC-Based Decoding for VLSF Codes in Hardcore-Regulated MAC arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper studies the decoding delay of variable-length stop-feedback (VLSF) codes with successive interference cancellation over multiple access channels. For deployments modeled by hardcore point processes, the SINR has a positive lower bound for all transmitters in the coverage region. Under a fixed total error probability constraint, these transmitters are decodable within an upper-bounded delay, which is well approximated by an inverse Gaussian distribution. Numerical results show that hardcore regulation provides uniform performance guarantees across links.

entry.title: Six families of binary codes from Ding's conjectures: proofs and counterexamples on code weights
entry.summary: Six Families of Binary Codes Arising from Ding's Conjectures arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 Ding proposed ten conjectures on binary linear codes built from Boolean functions, and four were already proved by Gölo\u{g}lu and Krasnayová. This paper studies the remaining six conjectures. It obtains common weight restrictions and infinite five-weight families for Conjectures 19 and 27, and shows that codes in Conjecture 30 have three, four, or five nonzero weights, with a four-weight example disproving the original claim. For Conjecture 34 it gives a general (2h+1)-weight bound and a six-weight counterexample, and Conjecture 37 is completely resolved.

entry.title: Exponential Backoff: Meta-Stability and Implicit Admission Control
entry.summary: Exponential Backoff: Meta-Stability and Implicit Admission Control arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper analyzes exponential backoff, an algorithm that lets several users share one communication channel in a distributed way, similar to networking standards like 802.11. The authors show the algorithm is meta-stable: over long time scales, the system oscillates between configurations where only a subset of sources effectively access the channel. This creates a form of implicit admission control. The paper provides theoretical tools and numerical experiments, which are fully reproducible, with code publicly available as a Python package.

entry.title: Windowed, Quantized Group ADMM for Distributed Optimization on Heterogeneous Edge Networks
entry.summary: Windowed and Quantized Group-Based ADMM for Distributed Optimization in Heterogeneous Edge Networks arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper proposes WQ-GADMM, a method that coordinates group-based updates of edge clients under limited activation capacity and communication resources. Clients are grouped by estimated computation time, a limited number of groups are activated per window, and the cloud updates the global model after every group has updated once, with quantized model exchanges in both directions. For smooth nonconvex objectives, the authors bound the average squared KKT residual, with a term decreasing in iterations and a quantization-dependent error term. Experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 show that 12-bit communication reduces communication volume and simulated wall-clock time while keeping test accuracy comparable to full precision.

entry.title: Cobalt: Using Expert Co-activation to Speed Up Distributed MoE Training
entry.summary: Cobalt: Leveraging Expert Co-activation for Efficient Distributed MoE Training arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper presents Cobalt, a training framework for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models. It observes that many pairs of experts are often activated together by the same tokens, and uses this to co-locate such experts on the same node, reducing cross-node traffic, while adjusting workloads within nodes at each step. A communication-aware task assignment method routes tokens to fewer remote nodes. On 32 B200 GPUs, the authors report speedups of 1.53 to 2.41 times (1.28 to 1.89 times on average) over existing frameworks and a 75.74% to 99.26% reduction in cross-node token traffic.

entry.title: Janus: Efficient agentic LLM serving with SSD-based sparse KV storage
entry.summary: Efficient Agentic LLM Serving over SSD-based Sparse KV Storage arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 The paper presents Janus, a serving framework for agentic LLM sessions that store history key-value caches on SSDs and use sparse attention. It runs the model's own KV selection module on earlier intermediate values to predict needed data, moving SSD reads off the inference critical path. It also coalesces reads and packs scattered writes to improve SSD efficiency. Across three models and three agentic traces, Janus reduces time to first token by up to 1.57-3.69 times over existing works while keeping decode efficiency.

entry.title: Reshaping Rollout Workloads for Asynchronous RL Post-Training on Heterogeneous Accelerators
entry.summary: Reshaping Rollout Workloads for Asynchronous RL Post-Training on Heterogeneous Accelerators arXiv · Sep 29, 2026 This paper addresses rollout scheduling for reinforcement learning post-training on heterogeneous hardware and presents CadenceRL. It reshapes the workload structurally, using pacing, concentration, and late-bound KV preparation, to balance aggregate decode throughput with per-trajectory completion time without manual routing configuration. The authors report up to 48% higher decode throughput and up to 64% lower P95 trajectory latency on heterogeneous rollout pools.

entry.title: Goal-oriented ordered autoencoder for progressive, successively refined communication
entry.summary: Goal-Oriented Ordered Autoencoding for Successive Refinement in Progressive Communication arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 The paper proposes GO-OAE, a progressively refinable quantized latent sequence optimized for downstream task utility rather than source reconstruction. Inference can be made from any received prefix of the code index sequence, with accuracy improving as more indices arrive. On MiniImageNet it reaches over 96% of the lossless upper-bound classification accuracy at 324 bits per image, and over 94% of the bound using only 70% of the indices.

entry.title: Knowing When to Hand Off: Critic-Guided Adaptive Execution for Cloud-Local Embodied Agents
entry.summary: Know When to Escalate: Critic-Guided Adaptive Execution for Cloud-Local Embodied Agents arXiv · Oct 22, 2026 This paper presents CARE, a framework in which a lightweight critic model monitors a local executor and hands control to a stronger cloud model when local execution becomes unreliable. A shared handoff memory keeps execution context so the cloud model can intervene without restarting. Across diverse embodied benchmarks, CARE raises task success by 6.3 to 18.3 percentage points over the strongest collaboration baseline while approaching or exceeding cloud-only success.

entry.title: Placing weights alone is not enough: synchronization limits multi-node CPU decoding of ternary LLMs
entry.summary: Weight Placement Is Not Enough: Synchronization in Multi-Node CPU Decoding of Ternary LLMs arXiv · Oct 21, 2026 The paper finds that ternary LLMs read only a few gigabytes per decoded token, yet on a dual-socket, four-NUMA-node server the fastest ternary runtime it tested uses less than half the memory bandwidth. Even with each weight placed on the node of the thread that reads it, threads spend much of each token waiting at synchronization points, mostly for the slowest threads on each node. On identical kernels, a Megatron-style column split beat a row-owned split in every configuration measured, with most of the gain from reduced waiting between threads. Where decoding is DRAM-bound, the resulting engine is 1.5-2.1x faster than ik_llama.

entry.title: Testing runtime prediction and safe walltime limits for supercomputer jobs
entry.summary: Evaluating Runtime Prediction and Conservative Walltime Policies in HPC Systems arXiv · Oct 20, 2026 This paper introduces SAFE, a framework that works with any runtime predictor and turns predicted runtimes into conservative, bounded walltime recommendations for HPC jobs. Its main contribution is this decision layer rather than a new prediction model. Tests on production job histories from Fugaku and NREL Eagle show that the approach reduces walltime gaps, while keeping job termination rates below 1% on both systems.

entry.title: AoI-aware polar code rate adaptation without channel estimation
entry.summary: AoI-Aware Polar Code Blind Rate Adaptation arXiv · Oct 20, 2026 This paper studies how to adaptively choose how many of the most reliable coordinates to use in polar-coded transmission, balancing age of information against throughput. The controller updates the prefix length using only the last decoding outcome, with no channel estimation. The authors derive a closed-form stationary distribution and exact steady-state AoI and goodput, and simulations on a 64-coordinate polar code over a binary symmetric channel are used to check these predictions. The paper also quantifies the goodput cost of adapting from one feedback bit compared with a genie-aided bound.

entry.title: GeoTrain: Energy-aware automatic parallelism for training AI models on mixed, geographically spread GPUs
entry.summary: GeoTrain: Energy-Aware Automatic Parallelism for Foundation Model Training on Heterogeneous Geo-Distributed Resources arXiv · Oct 19, 2026 This paper presents GeoTrain, a system for training foundation models across geographically distributed GPUs with differing compute, memory, power, and network capabilities. It jointly selects GPUs, partitions model layers, and sets pipeline configurations while optimizing both training time and energy use. Experiments with decoder-only Transformer models report that GeoTrain reduces iteration time and energy consumption compared with existing state-of-the-art approaches.

entry.title: Fault-tolerant task offloading for real-time apps at the mobile edge
entry.summary: Fault-Tolerant Offloading Framework for Real-Time Applications in Mobile Edge Computing arXiv · Oct 19, 2026 This paper studies deadline-constrained task offloading and resource allocation in mobile edge computing systems with backhaul networks, aiming to maximize total inference accuracy improvement. The problem is formulated as an integer linear program and shown to be NP-hard. The authors propose FastSA, a linear-time approximation algorithm, and a fault detection and recovery framework for backhaul link and edge server failures. Experiments use image classification workloads and real-world taxi traces.

entry.title: Information Bottleneck for Stable Variables: A Generalization of the Gaussian Case
entry.summary: On the Information Bottleneck for Stable Variables arXiv · Oct 6, 2026 This paper generalizes the Gaussian information bottleneck problem to jointly stable variables X and Y, where X = Y + A and A is stable and independent of Y. The authors derive optimal linear stable encoders of the form T = kX + N, giving a closed-form solution and critical value. They show that, except in the Gaussian case, such stochastic linear encoders are strictly suboptimal but become asymptotically optimal at large compression rates. The linear solution reduces to the classic Gaussian information bottleneck for jointly Gaussian variables.

entry.title: Two Communicating Robots Catching a Moving Target on Star Graphs
entry.summary: Capturing a Moving Target on Star Graphs by Two Communicating Mobile Agents arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 This paper studies searching for a moving target on an m-ray star graph, a generalization of linear search to several directions. The target is placed adversarially on one ray and moves at constant speed. Two robots cooperate under either a face-to-face communication model or an asymmetric sender-receiver model. The authors give upper bounds on the competitive ratio under three knowledge assumptions and derive lower bounds in some cases.

entry.title: NosRacer: Dynamic Detection of Race Conditions in On-Device Network Operating Systems
entry.summary: NosRacer: Dynamic Detection of Race Conditions in On-Device Network Operating Systems arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 This paper presents NosRacer, a dynamic analysis framework that detects race conditions in industrial on-device network operating systems, where asynchronous message ordering can cause configuration errors. It uses a two-phase design: a concentration phase that narrows analysis to relevant components and state variables, and a perturbation phase that alters message asynchrony to expose race-prone interleavings. The framework was implemented in a commercial NOS and tested on five key control-plane components.

entry.title: Delegating Pricing to Algorithms: Why Slower Learning Can Win
entry.summary: Delegate Pricing to Algorithms: When Slow and Steady Wins the Race arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 This paper studies how firms choose learning rates for pricing algorithms in a continuous-time pricing game. The authors model a meta-game where payoffs are the discounted sum of profits along the learning path. They find that under strategic substitutability firms prefer faster learning, while under strategic complementarity overly fast algorithms speed up rival responses and reduce transitional profits. The paper proves that firms design sluggish algorithms in equilibrium, even though convergence to the competitive price is guaranteed.

entry.title: Sorted mutability as an entropy-based measure: theory and two applications
entry.summary: Sorted Mutability as an Entropic Functional: Theory and Two Applications arXiv · Oct 6, 2026 The paper studies sorted mutability, a information-based quantity with an explicit entropic character. The authors show it is directly proportional to data diversity and can be expressed via Shannon entropies, linking compression-based measures to information theory. Unlike regular mutability, sorted mutability removes sequential ordering and characterizes the distribution of observed values. Applications include the two-dimensional ferromagnetic Q-clock model and wind-power production data.

entry.title: Coexponential Exploration in the Clef Programming Language
entry.summary: Coexponential Exploration in the Clef Programming Language arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 This paper describes the Clef concurrent language, whose compiler tracks state ownership, waiting computations and request dependencies. It models stateful services and client pools with a coexponential account and uses delimited continuations to retain what each interaction needs. The authors prove state-ownership and reply preservation and derive circular-wait exclusion under stated assumptions. These results aim to keep service composition correct when lowered to multiple hardware targets.

entry.title: Heuristics and machine learning for analyzing faults in distributed self-stabilizing programs
entry.summary: Efficient Heuristics and Machine Learning Approach for Fault Characterization in Distributed Self-Stabilizing Programs arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 The paper studies consistency violating faults, where a process reads stale shared-memory data, in self-stabilizing distributed programs. It proposes a conflicting-edges-based state-space exploration method for (Δ+1)-Graph Coloring and a machine learning model for a Maximal Independent Set program. The goal is to characterize when and where such faults occur to support runtime measures that improve efficiency.

entry.title: Indoor radio channel measurements at upper 6 GHz with directional and quasi-omnidirectional antennas
entry.summary: Directional and Quasi-Omnidirectional Indoor Channel Measurements at Upper 6 GHz arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper reports wideband indoor channel measurements in the upper 6 GHz band using directional and quasi-omnidirectional antenna pairs in a hall and a corridor. It fits path loss models for line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight conditions and characterizes shadow fading, RMS delay spread, and equivalent K factors. Directional links show smaller line-of-sight residuals and delay spread and higher equivalent K factors.

entry.title: A 1/2-approximation algorithm for Pandora's problem with deadlines
entry.summary: A 1/2-Approximation for Pandora's Problem with Deadlines arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper studies Pandora's problem with deadlines, a sequential search model where each box has a publicly known deadline for opening and selection. The authors prove that a simple threshold strategy achieves a 1/2-approximation to the optimal expected utility. This improves the previous guarantee, arbitrarily close to 1/4, due to Amanatidis et al. (2025).

entry.title: Large player classes and approximately weighted voting: a paper showing that simple games become close to weighted majority voting when each class of equivalent players is large
entry.summary: Large player classes and approximately weighted voting arXiv · Oct 7, 2026 The paper studies whether simple games admit weighted majority representations. It is known that completeness of the coalitional desirability relation does not guarantee such a representation, so the authors show that weightedness holds in an approximate sense. When all classes of equally desirable players grow large while their number stays bounded, the approximation error is O(1/n_min), a bound the authors show is tight.

entry.title: Cold-atom Rydberg array with time-space multiplexing for sensitive wireless receivers
entry.summary: Cold-Atom Rydberg Array with Spatiotemporal Multiplexing for High-Sensitivity Wireless Communications arXiv · Oct 6, 2026 This paper studies a cold-atom Rydberg array (CoRA) receiver designed to avoid thermal noise, Doppler broadening, and photon shot noise found in hot-vapor atomic receivers. It proposes spatiotemporal multiplexing (STM) for gap-free symbol sampling and a joint binomial particle smoother (JBPS) for signal detection. Numerical results show that STM removes the temporal sampling bottleneck and JBPS lowers the bit error rate. The authors also report a tradeoff: more atoms reduce quantum projection noise but lower the sustainable packet repetition rate.

entry.title: Signaling dimension of cross-polytopes: how many classical resources are needed to mimic them
entry.summary: On the signaling dimension of the cross-polytope arXiv · Oct 5, 2026 This paper studies the signaling dimension of cross-polytopes in the general probabilistic model of information theory. The signaling dimension is the smallest classical communication complexity needed to perfectly reproduce a system's input-output correlations. It was previously known to be 3 for three, four, and five dimensional cross-polytopes. The authors give logarithmic lower and upper bounds for higher dimensions, determining the value up to an additive gap of 2. The lower bound shows the signaling dimension grows without bound, unlike balls and hypercubes.

entry.title: Fair division of indivisible items via subsidies to achieve best-of-both-worlds guarantees
entry.summary: Best-of-Both-Worlds Fair Division via Subsidies arXiv · Oct 11, 2026 The paper studies how fair division with subsidies relates to best-of-both-worlds fairness for indivisible items. It proves that if every instance in a valuation class admits a fair allocation that can be made envy-free with subsidies, then an ex-ante envy-free lottery over such allocations exists. The result yields alternative proofs for additive goods, chores, and mixtures, and the converse holds for two agents but fails for three or more. ★★★★ Notable: Proves a general reduction linking BoBW existence to subsidized envy-freeability, with a counterexample and three-agent results; strong theory, narrow practical reach.

entry.title: Minimizing estimation error in wireless sensing by optimizing movable antenna array geometry
entry.summary: MSE Minimization for Movable Antenna Enhanced Wireless Sensing via Array Geometry Optimization arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper studies movable antenna (MA) arrays that adapt their geometry to reduce angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimation mean squared error (MSE) across arbitrary SNR levels. The authors derive a deterministic MSE approximation that captures both local mainlobe error and outlier error caused by sidelobes, and propose three MA structures suited to different hardware constraints. Numerical results show the approximation closely matches the true MSE and the proposed structures outperform CRB-optimized designs by orders of magnitude in the tested low-to-medium SNR range.

entry.title: AgentWeave: Efficient Distributed Agent Serving via Flow Decomposition
entry.summary: AgentWeave: Efficient Distributed Agent Serving via Flow Decomposition arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper presents AgentWeave, a distributed serving system for agent applications built from LLM calls and tool invocations. It uses an aggregated deployment and a flow decomposition mechanism that splits long agent requests into fine-grained execution units, so short and newly arriving requests are not stalled by long ones. Experiments on four representative agent applications report 1.81x higher throughput, 2.45x lower average latency, and 2.04x lower P90 latency than state-of-the-art baselines.

entry.title: Speeding up MoE training by jointly placing experts and coordinating replicas
entry.summary: Accelerating MoE Training through Expert Placement and Replica Coordination arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 Training sparse mixture-of-experts models across many devices is slowed by uneven workloads and all-to-all communication. This paper presents PlaceMoE, which jointly optimizes expert layout and token-to-replica mapping and overlaps replica gradient synchronization with attention backward passes. On 32-GPU and 64-NPU clusters using Qwen3-VL and DeepSeek-V3, it reports up to 6.94x faster all-to-all communication and 1.74 to 2.33x end-to-end training speedups over VeOmni.

entry.title: Energy-aware agent orchestration for deploying services across multiple sites
entry.summary: Energy-Aware Agentic Orchestration for Multi-Site Service Deployment arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper presents an orchestration framework that measures the energy used by LLM reasoning as part of its control loop, across a Kubernetes testbed spanning two European data centers. It compares single-shot tool calling, ReAct, and plan-and-execute strategies on ten natural-language intents. ReAct and plan-and-execute produced executable tool calls but required multiple LLM inferences, and prefix caching reduced mean ReAct GPU energy use by 29.4%.

entry.title: Maximizing sum rate in practical RIS-assisted rate-splitting multiple access systems
entry.summary: Sum Rate Maximization for Practical RIS-Enhanced Rate-Splitting Multiple Access Systems arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper studies how to maximize the multiuser sum rate in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) systems using rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA), accounting for the coupling between RIS phase and amplitude. To handle the resulting non-convex problem, the authors propose a variable separation algorithm that works with continuous phase shifts or any amplitude-phase coupling relationship and can extend to NOMA and OMA systems. Simulations show over 190% gain compared with an ideal-RIS benchmark, and the RSMA scheme significantly outperforms the corresponding NOMA and OMA schemes.

entry.title: Vesta: a queueing-aware scheduler for LLM serving on real workloads
entry.summary: Vesta: Queueing-Aware LLM Scheduling for Real-World Workloads arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper presents Vesta, a scheduler for distributed agentic LLM serving that accounts for queueing, cache locality, and KV cache transfer. Each session gets a stable holder for its authoritative KV cache, while each request's executor is chosen independently based on backlog and congestion. On real-world agentic workloads, Vesta improves throughput by 14.0% and reduces mean TTFT by 57.8% over the state-of-the-art scheduler in a PD-colocated deployment. In PD-disaggregated deployments, it reduces mean TTFT by up to 18.1% and P99 TTFT by up to 29.0% at matched throughput.

entry.title: Optimal receive beam design on the observation axis for RSMA satellite-UAV downlinks
entry.summary: Optimal Receive Design on the Observation Axis for RSMA Satellite-UAV Downlinks arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper studies receiver design for rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) downlinks from a satellite to a UAV, separating the receiver's observation state from the physical signal. The authors use a physical-observation dual-axis framework and show that, with known line-of-sight response and noise covariance, a noise-weighted matched combiner maximizes every decoding SINR and the minimum user rate. Under directional uncertainty, they characterize the optimal receive direction and mean array gain. For mean rate, they prove the RSMA common-rate water level is jointly concave in receive gains and derive a computable global upper bound.

entry.title: DeepTelecom: A differentiable framework for simulating wireless channels in changing, mixed environments
entry.summary: DeepTelecom: A Differentiable Multimodal Framework for Channel Twinning in Dynamic Heterogeneous Wireless Environments arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 The paper presents DeepTelecom, a material-aware, high-fidelity multimodal channel dataset and reproducible generation framework for wireless networks with UAVs and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces. A large language model maps scene surfaces to frequency-dependent electromagnetic parameters, and a differentiable GPU-accelerated Sionna ray tracer simulates propagation across several frequency bands. The authors report that in 3D UAV localization, the 90th-percentile error falls from 31.05 m to 2.43 m compared with channel-state-information-only schemes.

entry.title: Byzantine-tolerant single-writer register for GPU-style shared memory
entry.summary: Byzantine-linearizable Single-Writer Multi-Reader Register in the GPU-Inspired Shared Memory Model arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper studies whether atomic register semantics can be preserved in a GPU-inspired shared memory model when any thread, including the writer, may act Byzantine. It presents CAReg, which uses constant memory with a quantifiable probability of invalid reads, and SnapObject, which keeps a bounded window of authenticated writes to eliminate invalid reads. SnapObject tolerates up to n-1 Byzantine processes through lock-free and wait-free variants. The authors suggest that GPU phase-based, lock-step execution partially compensates for the lack of access control.

entry.title: UAV SAR imaging under non-ideal motion in ISAC systems using diffusion posterior sampling
entry.summary: UAV SAR Imaging via Diffusion Posterior Sampling under Non-Ideal Motion in ISAC Systems arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper studies synthetic aperture radar imaging from drones in low-altitude integrated sensing and communication systems, where non-ideal trajectories and unknown position errors cause severe image defocusing. The authors formulate imaging as an exact linear inverse problem and propose a diffusion posterior sampling framework for super-resolution, combined with joint motion compensation. Simulations report a PSNR above 21.3 dB even under half resolution truncation, and 23.65 dB with a position-error estimation residual of 0.19 cm under unknown motion errors.

entry.title: TurboProm: A Low-Cost, High-Performance Accelerator for Large-Scale Metrics Monitoring
entry.summary: TurboProm: Low Cost and High Performance Metrics Observability at Scale arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 Large cloud and enterprise systems use tools such as Prometheus to monitor metrics like CPU, memory, and network usage, but analyzing these at scale is costly and slow. This paper presents TurboProm, a backwards-compatible drop-in accelerator that analyzes semantic-preserving summaries instead of estimating query results directly from raw time-series data. The authors report significant reductions in query latency and cost compared with state-of-the-art solutions across diverse real and synthetic workloads. The implementation is open source.

entry.title: Low-latency LDPC decoding using consensus-based residual belief propagation
entry.summary: Low-Latency LDPC Decoding Based on Consensus and Return Residual Belief Propagation arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 The paper proposes two new decoding algorithms for LDPC codes, C&R-RBP and C&DR-RBP, to reduce the number of iterations needed to reach a target decoding error rate. Both keep the same residual calculation complexity as the original RBP algorithm. C&DR-RBP performs better in early iterations, making it suited to low-latency use. Simulations based on the 5G New Radio standard show both methods outperform competing RBP-based algorithms in frame error rate and bit error rate.

entry.title: Product selection under Mallows ranking preferences, with a faster approximation method
entry.summary: Assortment Optimization under the Mallows Model: Independent-Utility Choice Equivalence and Its Algorithmic Implications arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper studies assortment optimization, choosing which products to offer, when customer preferences follow the Mallows model, which describes rankings by their distance from a reference order. The authors show that Mallows choice probabilities can be exactly reproduced by a single collection of mutually independent random utilities, for every possible offered set. Using this representation together with an existing framework for independent random utilities, they derive a polynomial-size finite-support reduction and an approximation scheme running in time O(n^{Õ(1/ε²)}), allowing arbitrary prices, concentration parameters, and modal rankings. ★★★★ Notable: Uncovers independent-utility structure in Mallows choice, yielding a polynomial-time approximation scheme that improves on prior quasi-polynomial results with rigorous support.

entry.title: Orthogonal SC-LDPC codes for insertion, deletion and substitution channels
entry.summary: Orthogonal SC-LDPC Codes for the IDS Channel arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 The paper proposes a coding scheme for insertion, deletion and substitution (IDS) channels aimed at short DNA storage strands. It replaces an inner synchronisation code with a spatially coupled LDPC code spread across strands, so each decoded position serves as a synchronisation anchor. The authors bound the achievable rate and show that, for 100-nucleotide strands, the scheme outperforms a rate-matched concatenated construction.

entry.title: Sequential detection of when a transmitter switches between PSK modulation schemes, with controlled false alarms and delay
entry.summary: Sequential Change Point Detection for PSK Modulation Switching arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 Adaptive communication transmitters may switch modulation schemes at an unknown time, and receivers must detect the switch quickly without frequent false alarms. The paper studies sequential detection of switches between phase shift keying schemes over an additive white Gaussian noise channel, using CUSUM and MOSUM detectors built from the log-likelihood ratio and its low-SNR approximation. For a switch from QPSK to BPSK, the authors derive the moment-generating and probability density functions of the approximate statistic to relate the threshold to the average run length to false alarm and worst-case detection delay. Monte Carlo simulations show the derived expressions closely match empirical results across thresholds.</summary>

entry.title: Smoothed Polynomial-Time Algorithms for Deterministic Discounted-Sum and Mean-Payoff Games
entry.summary: Algorithms with Smoothed Polynomial-Time Complexity for Deterministic Discounted-sum and Mean-payoff Games arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper studies two-player zero-sum games on graphs with discounted-sum and mean-payoff objectives, a problem in NP ∩ coNP whose polynomial-time solvability remains open. The authors analyze a variant of strategy iteration with a new technique. They show it achieves smoothed polynomial complexity for general game graphs, not only ergodic ones. The guarantee is an expected runtime bound, strengthening earlier high-probability results. ★★★★ Notable: A new analysis technique removes the ergodicity restriction and upgrades high-probability to expected-runtime smoothed polynomial bounds, resolving an open problem; impact mainly within game theory an

entry.title: Quantum Annealing for Wireless Resource Allocation: A Guide to QUBO Modeling
entry.summary: Quantum Annealing for Resource Allocation in Next-Generation Wireless Communication Networks: A QUBO Modeling Guide arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 This paper provides guidelines for formulating wireless resource allocation problems as QUBO models for quantum annealing. It uses a small terrestrial-aerial example to show how a fractional SINR maximization objective is converted into a two-bit QUBO and decoded into a scheduling decision. The authors discuss encoding, constraint handling, hardware embedding and feasibility verification, and introduce a QUBO Compatibility Index as a diagnostic for formulation readiness. A case study on max-min uplink power control in cell-free massive MIMO is included.

entry.title: Weight enumerators of irreducible cyclic codes of length 2^ℓ
entry.summary: The weight enumerators of irreducible cyclic codes of length 2^ℓ arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 The paper uses a recently found spectral relation between irreducible cyclic codes and generalized Paley graphs to study the weight distribution of irreducible cyclic codes of length 2^ℓ. These codes were earlier studied by Sharma, Bakshi and Raka, who split them into two families with two cases each. The authors identify the associated generalized Paley graphs as complete, semiprimitive, Hamming, or Cartesian products of semiprimitive graphs, and compute their spectra. This yields explicit expressions for the weight enumerators of all such codes.

entry.title: WZIP and WLZ4: LZ77 compressors whose window size depends on match length
entry.summary: WZIP and WLZ4: LZ77 Codecs with Match-Length-Dependent Sliding Windows arXiv · Oct 8, 2026 The paper presents two LZ77-based compression formats, WLZ4, a byte-aligned LZ4-class format, and WZIP, an entropy-coded Zstandard-class format. Each match length gets its own sliding window, and the decoder infers the allowed offset range from the decoded length. On the Silesia corpus, WLZ4 reaches a compression ratio up to 16% above LZ4HC but decodes more slowly. WZIP exceeds the compression ratio of Zstandard 22, with its trusted decoder running at about 91% of Zstandard's speed.

entry.title: Demand-private coded caching with unequal file sizes and cache sizes: exact trade-off for two users and two files
entry.summary: Heterogeneous Demand-Private Coded Caching: Exact Characterization for Two Users and Two Files arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper studies coded caching where files and user cache capacities are heterogeneous and each user's demand must stay private from the other users. The authors extend the virtual-user reduction so that non-private schemes can be turned into demand-private ones under heterogeneous cache sizes. For two users and two files with arbitrary file sizes and cache capacities, they exactly characterize the memory-rate trade-off using eight linear inequalities, with achievable schemes and information-theoretic lower bounds.

entry.title: Limits of covertly serving extra jobs in a queue when Willie sees busy-period statistics
entry.summary: Fundamental Limits of Covert queueing under Busy-Period Observations arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 The paper studies a queueing system run by Bob that serves legitimate user Willie's jobs, while Bob tries to covertly serve additional Poisson-arriving jobs. Willie receives per-busy-period statistics, either the number of jobs served or the busy-period duration. Under either statistic, the maximum expected number of covert extra jobs scales as the square root of the number of busy periods. The associated scaling constant, called the covert queueing constant, is characterized for each statistic.

entry.title: Comparing Scheduling Methods for Cloud, Fog, and Edge Computing, with a Selection Guide
entry.summary: Scheduling in Cloud,Fog, and Edge Computing: A Comparative Analysis and Decision Framework for Technique Selection arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This review compares methods for scheduling tasks, jobs, and workflows across cloud, fog, and edge computing environments. It covers heuristic, metaheuristic, learning-based, and hybrid techniques, analyzing studies published between 2020 and 2026 by granularity, environment, objectives, constraints, metrics, and tools. The authors describe trade-offs among computational efficiency, optimization capability, adaptability, and implementation complexity across these families. They then propose a decision framework to help select a technique based on workload, environmental conditions, objectives, resource constraints, and computational requirements.

entry.title: A paper on GPU-resident execution that keeps sensor processing on the device to reduce timing jitter.
entry.summary: GPU-resident Execution for Timing-predictable Sensor Processing Systems arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper proposes GPU-resident Execution, a model that keeps sensor input and GPU processing in a long-lived device-resident loop so that no host CPU wakeups are needed. The authors implement it in NVIDIA's Holoscan C++ framework and evaluate it on NVIDIA GPUs and SoCs across several workloads. On a 1080p, 60 Hz camera-to-display application, photon-to-display jitter drops from 4.83 ms to 0.66 ms, and software-processing jitter drops from 1.70 ms to 0.01 ms, compared with a CPU-driven GPU-memory RDMA baseline.

entry.title: Asymmetric Information in Dynamic Lending Games
entry.summary: Asymmetric Information in Dynamic Lending Games arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper studies a dynamic lending game in which supply is limited but reusable, and borrower arrivals and loan durations are random. It compares how disclosing rivals' aggregate available supply to all, some, or no lenders affects payoffs. The authors find that asymmetric disclosure can raise total lender payoffs while total lending stays the same, and that which lenders receive the information matters.

entry.title: Distortion of voting to pick several winners when voters give only coarse thresholds
entry.summary: The Distortion of Threshold Approval Multiwinner Voting arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper studies multiwinner voting, where n voters and m candidates are used to select a committee of size k. Voters report only coarse information based on t utility thresholds rather than exact cardinal utilities. The authors give upper bounds on distortion for deterministic and randomized rules, and norm-dependent lower bounds that match them asymptotically for constant committee sizes.

entry.title: Computational Complexity of Autobidding Equilibria in GSP Sponsored Shopping Auctions
entry.summary: Complexity of Autobidding Equilibria in GSP Sponsored Shopping arXiv · Oct 10, 2026 This paper revisits autobidding equilibria in GSP sponsored shopping auctions, following Dütting et al. It shows that equilibria exist under both budget constraints (ABE-B) and return-on-investment constraints (ABE-R), and that they always admit polynomial-size support over the allocation space. Exact equilibria are shown to be computable in FIXP, approximate equilibria in PPAD, and computing approximate equilibria is PPAD-hard for both models.

entry.title: Benchmarking Content-Defined Chunking Algorithms for Data Deduplication
entry.summary: Benchmarking Content-Defined Chunking Algorithms for Data Deduplication arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 This paper isolates and compares eight base content-defined chunking algorithms used in data deduplication across four realistic workloads, measuring throughput, deduplication ratio, mean chunk size, and chunk-size variance. It derives formulas linking parameters of AE, RAM, and MII to expected chunk size. The authors find a long-standing error in the widely used AE parameterization that yields chunks 13-39% smaller than intended and inflates AE's reported deduplication.

entry.title: Privacy mechanism design with χ² utility under a bounded α-lift leakage constraint
entry.summary: On Privacy Mechanism Design Under a Bounded α-Lift Leakage Constraint with χ²-Utility arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 This paper studies designing a statistical privacy mechanism under a bounded α-lift leakage constraint. An agent releases U based on useful data Y, which is correlated with private data X, aiming to maximize Pearson χ² information while satisfying a point-wise privacy constraint. The authors derive a closed-form quadratic surrogate, an explicit feasible binary mechanism, and utility-gap bounds, and extend the results to point-wise Rényi-divergence privacy with numerical evaluation.

entry.title: How far Kolmogorov-Loveland randomness is from Martin-Löf randomness
entry.summary: How far is Kolmogorov-Loveland randomness from Martin-Löf randomness? arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 The paper studies maps called encodings that send basic sets to clopen sets while preserving uniform Lebesgue measure and disjointness. It asks whether a computable encoding can send every non-Martin-Löf-random sequence to sequences that fail a given randomness notion. The authors show no such encoding exists for partial computable randomness, but one exists for Kolmogorov-Loveland randomness, together with two non-monotonic betting strategies, at least one of which wins on every image sequence.

entry.title: Neural polar codes for source compression learned directly from data
entry.summary: Neural Polar Codes for Source Coding arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 This paper proposes a data-driven approach to lossless and lossy source compression based on polar codes. Neural polar decoders are trained directly from data to approximate conditional distributions of polar coordinates, without requiring an explicit source model. These learned distributions are used to estimate entropy rates, mutual information, and rate-distortion functions, and to build explicit polar compression schemes. Experiments show that the learned decoders closely match analytical successive-cancellation decoders when those are available, and remain usable when conventional methods are computationally infeasible or the source model is unknown.

entry.title: CompileMask: A method balancing expressiveness and efficiency in attention masking
entry.summary: CompileMask: Bridging the Gap Between Expressiveness and Efficiency in Attention Masking arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 The paper notes that modern attention workloads need diverse masks depending on runtime metadata, but efficient kernels support only a few patterns. It presents CompileMask, which uses an offline compiler to analyze visibility rules and generate mask-specific preprocessing kernels, with rules written in a region-based DSL called MaskSpec. At runtime, the generated kernel produces a compact Execution Descriptor so the attention kernel can check visibility by comparing element indices against precomputed endpoints. Experiments show up to 3.8× speedup over state-of-the-art methods.

entry.title: Ember: a framework making GPU unified virtual memory practical for oversubscribed workloads
entry.summary: Ember: Making Unified Virtual Memory Practical for Discrete-Memory GPUs arXiv · Oct 9, 2026 GPU working sets now exceed GPU memory, so applications must oversubscribe it and keep only hot data on the GPU. This paper presents Ember, a UVM management framework that uses a hybrid address space, counter-driven region promotion, and decay-based eager reclamation to improve performance without hints, profiling, or application changes. At 1.5x oversubscription, it is reported to be 6.8 to 10.6 times faster than UVM on six applications across three PCIe GPUs.
